rW5JtLRcNW.problem: Jointly learning an embedded signal and its reader from real editing outcomes is hard when closed-source editors allow forward queries but not backpropagation.
rW5JtLRcNW.method: EditInk alternates two phases: train the developer on actual edits of protected images with the ink fixed, then hold the developer fixed and optimize the ink using a protected view and differentiable simulated degradation views. Deployment uses shared ink and a single-image reader.
rW5JtLRcNW.key_idea: Alternating cooperative learning: fit the developer to actual editor outputs, then update the ink through the frozen developer using differentiable simulated edits, avoiding editor backpropagation.
rW5JtLRcNW.evidence: Experiments with actual editor outputs, including API editors on HumanEdit, against baselines such as WAM, with component ablations (per reviews).
rW5JtLRcNW.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract.
rW5JtLRcNW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practical for forward-only editors, trains without editor gradients, and is evaluated on actual editor outputs rather than composited regions.
rW5JtLRcNW.main_concern: The central ablation table appears to match the per-image-PGD results rather than the shared-ink setting, so component gains cannot be attributed reliably, and unseen API editors are untested.

hfR8LRyTlp.one_liner: Verifies agent actions by predicting intended effects, hypothesizing how they could be wrong, and testing those hypotheses before executing.
hfR8LRyTlp.problem: Confirmation-oriented action verification has a blind spot: a wrong action often passes every check that asks whether it is right.
hfR8LRyTlp.method: BlackSwan runs an expect-suspect-test procedure: it predicts the intended effect of each state-mutating action, formulates specific testable hypotheses for how it could be wrong, tests them with existing observations or additional non-mutating actions, and executes the action only if none survives testing.
hfR8LRyTlp.key_idea: Verify by refutation: generate testable failure hypotheses for each state-mutating action and execute only if none of them survives testing.
hfR8LRyTlp.evidence: Challenging AppWorld tasks, with transfer to other benchmarks (WebShop and ALFWorld per reviews), five backbones with and without thinking mode, and ablations.
hfR8LRyTlp.claimed_gains: Improves success rate over the strongest baseline on AppWorld by 14.9 and 25.2%p with and without the backbone model's thinking mode, respectively.
hfR8LRyTlp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shift from confirming to refuting actions is a clear, well-motivated idea with strong, consistent gains across benchmarks and backbones.
hfR8LRyTlp.main_concern: Compute overhead is large (about 6.4 times the tokens and 9.4 times the cost of ReAct) with no budget-matched baseline, so part of the gain may come from extra compute.

qNvg5trCv2.one_liner: Selective safety defense that re-scores uncertain requests with one learned intent token and deliberates only on those still uncertain.
qNvg5trCv2.problem: Selective defenses use a probe merely as a gate, sending confidently harmful and uncertain requests to the same costly deliberation, although most errors lie in the low-confidence region.
qNvg5trCv2.method: RESTATE refuses confidently harmful requests and answers confidently benign ones. For uncertain requests it appends a learned intent token and the same classifier rescores the representation at that token; only requests that remain uncertain are deliberated, and the LLM stays frozen.
qNvg5trCv2.key_idea: Append a single trainable embedding to uncertain inputs so the existing probe reads a refined representation, leaving the frozen LLM's generation unchanged.
qNvg5trCv2.evidence: Qwen3-8B on WildJailbreak, averaged over six inference-time defenses, plus other models (Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-20B per reviews) and external datasets.
qNvg5trCv2.claimed_gains: Reassessing uncertain requests raises the classifier's balanced accuracy by 7.1%p on Qwen3-8B with WildJailbreak, and averaged over six defenses attack success falls from 37.7% to 10.2% and over-refusal from 13.7% to 7.2% relative to always deliberating.
qNvg5trCv2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is well motivated by observed failure modes, modular and parameter-efficient, and combines with existing inference-time defenses.
qNvg5trCv2.main_concern: Gains shrink outside the main setting (about 1.1 balanced-accuracy points on Qwen3-32B and GPT-OSS-20B), and the single-token mechanism is not clearly isolated from simpler suffix or training effects.

OODcrxFiZw.one_liner: Selects transformer blocks to remove by how much removal hurts in-context learning, as a cheap predictor of post-repair quality.
OODcrxFiZw.problem: Depth-pruning criteria score damage before repair and cannot tell which of two equally damaging removals repair will undo, while testing every candidate set is infeasible.
OODcrxFiZw.method: Each candidate removal is scored by the drop in in-context learning ability, using a few forward passes, motivated by the view that in-context learning is an implicit weight update; the pruned model is then repaired. The study is extended to vision-language models.
OODcrxFiZw.key_idea: Use loss of demonstration-conditioned (in-context) performance as a proxy for how well the remaining layers can still learn during repair.
OODcrxFiZw.evidence: Over 1.6K prune-and-repair runs on five language models under two repair objectives, plus vision-language models.
OODcrxFiZw.claimed_gains: At 25% removal it has the best five-model average under both repair objectives, even ahead of a baseline that briefly fine-tunes every candidate, for a few percent of the pipeline cost.
OODcrxFiZw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the ICL probe predicts post-repair quality beyond present-damage scores, supported by the large prune-and-repair study and controls on demonstrations.
OODcrxFiZw.main_concern: Per-model gains are modest and uneven, and the experiments do not establish the claimed mechanism that the probe measures the remaining weights' ability to learn.

FRbun5b5GA.one_liner: In-context neurofeedback tests whether LLMs control activation-derived scores, with a separate writer model isolating task competence from access.
FRbun5b5GA.problem: Activation probes assume models cannot control what their activations encode, yet prior neurofeedback studies on language models conflict and no design separates task competence from genuine access to one's own activations.
FRbun5b5GA.method: A subject model maximizes or minimizes an activation-derived score shown back to it each turn. In one experiment the subject writes the scored sentences, in another a writer model writes them while the score comes from the subject's activations, and a fixed-sentence experiment tests control while processing.
FRbun5b5GA.key_idea: Decouple the model that writes text from the model whose activations are scored, so competence at the task is separated from privileged control over activations.
FRbun5b5GA.evidence: Ten open-weight models from five families with sizes from 9B to 32B; reviews report 42 readouts, two depths, disclosure conditions and 168,000 sessions.
FRbun5b5GA.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; some models move their own scores considerably but no more than a writer of comparable competence, indicating weak, model-dependent control that cannot yet fool monitors.
FRbun5b5GA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the writer/subject decoupling is an improved experimental control that clarifies an ambiguity in prior work and that effect sizes are reported conservatively.
FRbun5b5GA.main_concern: Observed effects are small (a 1.8-point shift, about 2% of the scale, in the fixed-sentence experiment), with limited mechanistic analysis and incremental insight over prior fixed-output neurofeedback work.

voHMm9u5LN.one_liner: Fuses sequence, evolutionary and structural views over spatial neighborhoods, with a catalytic partner retrieval auxiliary task, to rank catalytic residues.
voHMm9u5LN.problem: Catalytic residue prediction remains inaccurate for enzymes with few annotated homologs.
voHMm9u5LN.method: EnzyFuse predicts catalytic residues from each of three views (sequence, evolutionary, structural) so every view gets a direct learning signal, then combines the views over spatially neighboring residues. A training-only catalytic partner retrieval task uses existing annotations to identify other catalytic residues near an annotated one.
voHMm9u5LN.key_idea: Combine per-view residue predictions through structure-guided message passing over spatial neighbors, and add a training-only task retrieving catalytic partners near an annotated residue.
voHMm9u5LN.evidence: Splits jointly controlled for sequence and structural similarity, baselines retrained on the same data including a multi-model ensemble, three seeds with confidence intervals and ablations; reviewers cite AUPRC 0.7568 for EnzyFuse versus 0.7012 for the Squidly ensemble.
voHMm9u5LN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the careful joint sequence-structure split with leakage controls, baselines retrained on the same data, and consistent AUPRC gains.
voHMm9u5LN.main_concern: Novelty and low-homology evidence are limited: the design combines established components, and component gains on the no-neighbor subset are small (0.004 and 0.009 AUPRC) and lack confidence intervals.

54ZANwAVdh.one_liner: CoHuB is a simulation benchmark of 10 multi-humanoid collaboration tasks with VR-teleoperated demonstrations and egocentric observations.
54ZANwAVdh.problem: Existing humanoid benchmarks focus on single-humanoid skills and do not evaluate multi-humanoid collaboration under egocentric visual observations.
54ZANwAVdh.method: It provides 10 tasks (eight with two humanoids, two with three) covering patterns such as object handovers and jointly carrying large objects, plus synchronized demonstrations collected through multi-operator VR teleoperation where each operator controls one humanoid from its egocentric view.
54ZANwAVdh.key_idea: Collect synchronized multi-humanoid demonstrations with one VR operator per humanoid in egocentric view, across tasks varying base movement and physical coupling.
54ZANwAVdh.evidence: Experiments with representative visuomotor policies (decentralized, centralized and CTDE variants including foundation-model policies, per reviews) with phase-level evaluation.
54ZANwAVdh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a gap with a carefully specified, diverse task suite, useful demonstration data and broad baseline coverage.
54ZANwAVdh.main_concern: Baselines run under different information regimes, physical feasibility (object masses, friction, torque limits) is under-specified, and there is no formal problem statement or statistical significance reporting.

s9FiuJ4vS5.one_liner: Organizes original and LLM-expanded features into overlapping semantic subspaces and learns cross-dataset weights to aggregate their anomaly predictions.
s9FiuJ4vS5.problem: With very few labels, LLM-expanded tabular features enlarge the learning space, so detectors may confuse spurious relationships with real anomaly mechanisms.
s9FiuJ4vS5.method: LENS-AD groups original and knowledge-expanded features into overlapping semantic subspaces, each encoding a candidate anomaly mechanism. It learns a mapping from subspace descriptors to aggregation weights across source datasets and uses it to combine predictions without target validation labels.
s9FiuJ4vS5.key_idea: Use LLM knowledge to constrain how expanded features are used: semantic subspaces per candidate anomaly mechanism, weighted by a meta-learned mapping from subspace descriptors.
s9FiuJ4vS5.evidence: 20 real-world tabular anomaly detection benchmarks under few-labeled-anomaly and few-sample settings, with component ablations, random-subspace and stacking comparisons, and LLM and base-predictor robustness analyses.
s9FiuJ4vS5.claimed_gains: Competitive performance on 20 benchmarks under few-labeled-anomaly and few-sample settings, without target validation labels; no numeric margins visible in the abstract.
s9FiuJ4vS5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of using domain semantics under label scarcity is relevant and the pipeline is coherent, with ablations and analyses across LLMs and base predictors.
s9FiuJ4vS5.main_concern: Novelty looks incremental over LLM feature engineering, SemanticMask, and cross-task meta-learning such as MetaOD, the transferability of aggregation weights is assumed, and baselines such as AnoLLM are not compared.

CyaKIq7JYk.one_liner: Tests whether allocating dynamic-sparse-training sparsity by layer energy helps, measuring GPU energy across three execution back ends.
CyaKIq7JYk.problem: It is unclear whether energy-aware layer-wise sparsity allocation actually reduces training energy in dynamic sparse training, since savings depend on kernels and architecture.
CyaKIq7JYk.method: EA-DST initializes layer-wise sparsity from estimated energy and gives heavily pruned, high-energy layers a higher probability of slight regrowth. An identity bounds what any layer-wise allocation can save, and hardware-counter measurements test it on two CIFAR-10 CNNs.
CyaKIq7JYk.key_idea: Allocate sparsity by energy per weight rather than total layer energy, since savings equal the drop in average cost per weight when weights move to cheaper layers.
CyaKIq7JYk.evidence: Randomized-block GPU energy measurements with hardware counters on three execution back ends, on AlexNet and VGG-16 trained on CIFAR-10, plus an analytic identity bounding allocation savings.
CyaKIq7JYk.claimed_gains: Under cuSPARSE kernels on AlexNet, 9-20% less energy than uniform allocation and 0.90-1.02 points more accurate at equal energy on a laptop GPU (0.65-0.75 points at alpha=0.5 on three data-center GPUs), with no change on VGG-16.
CyaKIq7JYk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the value lies in measuring real hardware energy rather than FLOPs, and that the per-weight cost and regrowth analysis explains both the potential savings and the failure modes.
CyaKIq7JYk.main_concern: The controlled study is narrow: one laptop GPU measuring only GPU energy, two small CIFAR-10 CNNs, and short schedules, so findings may not transfer to other hardware or longer training.

GZowsf63Bh.one_liner: Shows short salience cues inserted into long contexts shift LLM retrieval toward marked key-value memories among similar distractors.
GZowsf63Bh.problem: Long-context retrieval fails when similar memories compete, and it is unclear whether textual salience cues can shift retrieval priority.
GZowsf63Bh.method: Builds a controlled key-value framework with random bindings and similar-key distractors, tests threat, reward, empathy, and importance cues on five open-weight LLMs, and analyzes layer-wise attention to target versus distractor values.
GZowsf63Bh.key_idea: Cue text marking a memory raises attention to its target value and lowers attention to distractors in mid-to-late layers, tilting target-distractor selection.
GZowsf63Bh.evidence: Five open-weight LLMs on controlled key-value retrieval, extended to LoCoMo-derived dialogue retrieval, with internal layer and attention analysis.
GZowsf63Bh.claimed_gains: Well-placed cues improve retrieval accuracy by roughly 30-60 percentage points in most models.
GZowsf63Bh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled design (random bindings, similar-key distractors, paired interventions) well isolating, with large effects across multiple models.
GZowsf63Bh.main_concern: Results rest on a synthetic key-value setting, the cause of the failure and of the cue effect is not explained, and the baseline lacks matched neutral markers to separate salience from formatting effects.

7mVeTd3Nlf.one_liner: Audio question-answering benchmark that turns textual-prior answers into distractors so correct answers require audio evidence.
7mVeTd3Nlf.problem: Audio QA accuracy may reflect textual priors rather than audio processing, since many questions are still answered correctly when audio is replaced with random noise.
7mVeTd3Nlf.method: MMALR is a multi-domain, multi-task benchmark using counter-prior construction: each correct answer is anchored in audio evidence and plausible textual predictions become distractors. It evaluates open- and closed-source large audio-language models and human participants.
7mVeTd3Nlf.key_idea: Counter-prior construction: make the answer that text alone suggests a distractor and anchor the correct answer in audio evidence.
7mVeTd3Nlf.evidence: Evaluation of open- and closed-source LALMs and humans, with paired normal-audio, noise, and silence conditions; the abstract is cut off before the results.
7mVeTd3Nlf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree text-solvability is a genuine problem in audio-model evaluation and that the construction, paired noise/silence/normal evaluation, and human quality checks are useful.
7mVeTd3Nlf.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the effect of counter-prior construction, and below-chance accuracy under noise is guaranteed by design and could itself be an exploitable bias.

BAsFjPESSt.one_liner: Causal interventions show CoT arithmetic digits are either copied from earlier computation or recomputed, depending on the receiver's state.
BAsFjPESSt.problem: A language model can copy a wrong intermediate result even when it can compute the correct one, and the mechanism behind this behavior was unclear.
BAsFjPESSt.method: A causal study of intermediate arithmetic in three Qwen3 and Ministral models uses internal readouts, activation patching, attention cuts, and value substitutions to separate a copy route from an operand-based recompute route.
BAsFjPESSt.key_idea: Early reads from the equals sign gate whether the receiver uses its own computation; late reads deliver the digit and can override it.
BAsFjPESSt.evidence: Causal interventions on three models from the Qwen3 and Ministral families; reviewers cite equals-sign value substitutions on fixed Cramer's-rule prefixes with two-digit answers.
BAsFjPESSt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that attention cuts and value substitutions give stronger causal evidence than activation probes alone and separate readable from used intermediate results.
BAsFjPESSt.main_concern: The scope is narrow (two model families, fixed prefixes, two-digit answers) and the positioning against prior arithmetic-probing and verification work is unclear.

MsX014tAvl.one_liner: Compares provenance graphs for repairing stale persistent agent memory, separating structural lineage from stored-state error.
MsX014tAvl.problem: When a source fact is corrected, stored conclusions may remain active and mislead later answers, and it is unclear whether reliable repair needs the full structural lineage.
MsX014tAvl.method: They distinguish historical dependency, update sensitivity, and stored-state error, and compare provenance graphs under a fixed repair operator in controlled memory lifecycles and public multi-hop tasks. A certificate, a subset of parent values sufficient to force the stored conclusion, explains which edges can be omitted, with consistency proofs for sequential and simultaneous corrections.
MsX014tAvl.key_idea: A certificate, the subset of parent values sufficient to force a stored conclusion, shows repair needs only update-sensitive support edges and not all structural descendants.
MsX014tAvl.evidence: Controlled memory lifecycles (about 50 synthetic episodes with Boolean rules per a reviewer), closed-loop runs, matched-random graph controls, and public lookup chains.
MsX014tAvl.claimed_gains: LLM material-support provenance reaches 95-100% of stale state while covering only about half of structural descendants, versus about two-thirds for matched-random graphs, and on public lookup chains LLM attribution is within 0.02 of oracle path repair.
MsX014tAvl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating provenance fidelity from repair adequacy is a useful distinction, with controlled comparisons showing edge-level scores alone are insufficient.
MsX014tAvl.main_concern: Evidence comes from narrow controlled settings (unate rules, binary answers, shallow chains, synthetic episodes) and lacks comparison with prior agent memory repair work.

5h9onpIjJ2.one_liner: Differentiable single decision tree whose splits sum learned univariate feature responses, with gating and exact subtree folding.
5h9onpIjJ2.problem: Simple splits need large trees to represent nonlinear boundaries, while generic multivariate node functions obscure how individual features affect routing.
5h9onpIjJ2.method: CAST forms each split by summing learned univariate responses built from node-specific combinations of a shared nonlinear basis and direct linear terms. Stochastic gates sparsify the features used at each node, and exact folding replaces constant subtrees with leaves.
5h9onpIjJ2.key_idea: Split scores are sums of per-feature nonlinear responses, giving nonlinear boundaries with an exact feature-wise decomposition of the routing score.
5h9onpIjJ2.evidence: A 20-dataset benchmark against 12 methods, a fixed-depth comparison at starting depths three to six, and plots of learned nodes.
5h9onpIjJ2.claimed_gains: Lowest mean rank of 1.675 among the 12 methods evaluated on every dataset, first rank at starting depths three through six, and exact folding removes 30.3% of internal nodes in aggregate while preserving predictions.
5h9onpIjJ2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the additive-split design is clean and can give more accurate trees than traditional decision trees, with strong and reasonably extensive empirical results.
5h9onpIjJ2.main_concern: Interpretability and compactness claims are weakly supported: soft routing uses all paths, comparisons with hard trees, CART or matched node budgets are missing or unfair, and the shared nonlinear basis network cost is not counted.

svvZ1w0qbA.one_liner: Frozen time series foundation models forecast from raw, cycle-residual, trend-residual, and subseries views, then select and aggregate candidates.
svvZ1w0qbA.problem: How to use extra inference compute effectively for frozen time series foundation models is unclear, and repeated sampling from a fixed input representation gives diminishing returns.
svvZ1w0qbA.method: A structured multi-view framework generates forecasts from raw contexts, cycle-residual and trend-residual representations, and temporal subseries; completed historical windows guide candidate selection and compact aggregation without updating model weights.
svvZ1w0qbA.key_idea: Diversify the input representation (raw, cycle-residual, trend-residual, subseries) rather than only resampling outputs, and pick top candidates by error on completed historical windows.
svvZ1w0qbA.evidence: Seven TSFMs, spanning stochastic and direct-quantile prediction, on all 97 GIFT-Eval tasks, with MASE, controlled Moirai analyses, and a historical profiling study for compact view pools.
svvZ1w0qbA.claimed_gains: Multi-view top-3 reduces aggregate MAE by 4.76% over historically selected raw-input ensembles and 2.10% over default inference; compact view pools retain about 85% of the full pool's MAE gain with 17.4% fewer prediction branches.
svvZ1w0qbA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the test-time scaling question for TSFMs is new and the experimental design, with historically selected raw baselines and matched controls, is rigorous and yields useful findings.
svvZ1w0qbA.main_concern: As an empirical study without a clear method, the takeaways are fragmented and not actionable (what helps depends on model, series, and selector), novelty is limited, and model and series coverage is questioned as narrow.

DXeChT9fBB.one_liner: Feeding PINN training diagnostics and run-level experience into an LLM-guided evolutionary loop jointly optimizes coupled PDE solver configurations.
DXeChT9fBB.problem: Effective physics-informed neural network configurations vary across PDEs, and existing automated search methods struggle to turn observed training behavior into cumulative improvements across coupled components.
DXeChT9fBB.method: PINNForge initializes diverse PINN configurations from PDE prior knowledge, executes them, and feeds retained elite configurations, training diagnostics, and accumulated run-level experience back to an LLM. Within a generate-execute-evaluate-evolve loop, the LLM revises and recombines representation, architecture, sampling, constraint, loss, and optimization choices.
DXeChT9fBB.key_idea: Use observed PINN training diagnostics and accumulated cross-generation run experience to guide an LLM-driven evolutionary search over coupled PINN architecture, sampling, loss, and optimization components.
DXeChT9fBB.evidence: Evaluated across 25 PDE benchmarks against RoPINN, PINNsFormer, PINNsAgent, and Lang-PINN, with component ablations removing knowledge guidance, execution feedback, or evolutionary search.
DXeChT9fBB.claimed_gains: Across 25 PDE benchmarks, PINNForge achieves the lowest mean MSE on 24 tasks, and removing knowledge guidance, execution feedback, or evolutionary search raises median task-wise MSE ratios to 3.74×, 12.10×, and 10.10×.
DXeChT9fBB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the broad empirical evaluation across 25 heterogeneous PDE benchmarks and informative component ablations.
DXeChT9fBB.main_concern: Reviewers highlight overfitting risk from reusing the same reference points for search selection and final MSE reporting without held-out test points, alongside limited methodological distinction from prior agentic PINN design loops.

FwNyRCul6v.one_liner: Jacobian lenses on multi-solution reasoning tasks probe low-rank latent subspaces separating solution validity from branch identity.
FwNyRCul6v.problem: It remains unclear whether reasoning models internally form a compact, repeatedly accessed workspace channel and how constraint enforcement differs between recursive latent and autoregressive architectures.
FwNyRCul6v.method: The authors fit Jacobian lenses at corpus, per-question, and per-solution levels on verifiable multi-solution mathematical reasoning tasks and perform subspace ablations in a recursive latent reasoner and an autoregressive LLM. Multi-solution tasks let interventions distinguish losing the ability to produce a valid solution from switching which valid solution is returned.
FwNyRCul6v.key_idea: Fit multi-level Jacobian lenses on multi-solution reasoning tasks and ablate low-rank latent subspaces to separate directions governing solution validity from directions selecting a specific solution.
FwNyRCul6v.evidence: Applied to a recursive latent reasoner (GRAM) and an autoregressive LLM (Qwen3-32B) on verifiable multi-solution puzzles including n-queens completion and cubic-graph edge coloring.
FwNyRCul6v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value using multi-solution mathematical puzzles to cleanly separate answer validity from solution identity and praise the careful probing methodology.
FwNyRCul6v.main_concern: Reviewers argue that finding causally sensitive low-rank Jacobian subspaces does not establish Global Workspace Theory properties, and note unmatched intervention procedures and training regimes between GRAM and Qwen3-32B.

8y0VmfxbAl.one_liner: Global trajectory memory, local event selection, and evidence-rewarded GRPO ground clinical EHR predictions in cited findings.
8y0VmfxbAl.problem: Clinical question answering over structured electronic health record code sequences requires combining full-trajectory context with accurately cited local clinical events that support the prediction.
8y0VmfxbAl.method: GLoC-EHR encodes structured EHR sequences into a fixed-size global trajectory memory aligned via hospital-course summaries and a local memory of selected events aligned via masked concept descriptions. Rationale fine-tuning followed by GRPO rewards both answer correctness and record-supported evidence citations.
8y0VmfxbAl.key_idea: Combine text-aligned global trajectory and local event memories with GRPO rewards for answer accuracy and record-supported evidence citations.
8y0VmfxbAl.evidence: Evaluations on MIMIC-IV outcome tasks and EHRSHOT cross-site transfer measure macro AUROC and evidence support alongside local-memory, cited-slot masking, and training-stage ablations.
8y0VmfxbAl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding structured EHR predictions in cited record findings is practically important and commend the anti-gaming GRPO reward design and masking ablations.
8y0VmfxbAl.main_concern: All three reviewers note that lexical-match rewards do not ensure clinical semantic faithfulness and that removing or masking the local memory route leaves predictive macro AUROC unchanged despite substantial added complexity.

HEIqsXlTGu.one_liner: Jointly decomposes brain responses and language model representations via crosscoders to classify features as shared or system-specific.
HEIqsXlTGu.problem: Prior brain-encoding studies show that language models predict neural responses to language, but do not identify which individual features are shared versus specific to either system.
HEIqsXlTGu.method: Brain-LM crosscoders decompose human fMRI responses and language model representations into a shared dictionary of latent features, labeling each feature as shared, brain-specific, or LM-specific from its predictive contribution to each modality. Automated feature explanations then generate hypotheses about concepts encoded by only one system.
HEIqsXlTGu.key_idea: Decompose brain activity and language model activations into a joint sparse feature set and partition features by their relative predictive contribution to each modality.
HEIqsXlTGu.evidence: Applied to open fMRI datasets recorded while human participants listened to naturalistic stories paired with language model representations.
HEIqsXlTGu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the crosscoder formulation is clearly presented and offers an intuitive methodological approach for decomposing brain-LM representational overlap.
HEIqsXlTGu.main_concern: Reviewers find the scientific interpretations and case-study insights weakly validated, noting that explained-variance splits and automated descriptions on single brain-LM pairs do not convincingly establish semantic divergence.

E1Dr1fedor.one_liner: Partitions planned views via tri-state masking and observation-anchored depth recovery for progressive sparse-view Gaussian splatting.
E1Dr1fedor.problem: Generative priors used in sparse-view 3D reconstruction can hallucinate content that conflicts with input images, degrading geometry and appearance in reliably observed regions.
E1Dr1fedor.method: GenAnchor plans coverage-aware camera trajectories toward under-reconstructed areas and partitions each planned view into preservation, refinement, and generation regions via tri-state masking for selective generative repair. It then estimates depth from repaired RGB sequences anchored by real observations and integrates the resulting RGB-D views into a global Gaussian splatting representation iteratively.
E1Dr1fedor.key_idea: Combine coverage-aware view planning, tri-state regional masking for selective generative supervision, and observation-anchored depth re-estimation in a progressive reconstruction loop.
E1Dr1fedor.evidence: Evaluated on multiple public 3D reconstruction datasets including ScanNet++ and Replica across observed and unobserved scene regions.
E1Dr1fedor.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well organized, targets a real failure mode in generative 3D reconstruction, and improves rendering and surface geometry across multiple datasets.
E1Dr1fedor.main_concern: Reviewers highlight biased evaluation from selecting the best of three runs by test-view PSNR on Replica and confounded comparisons due to bundled ablations and differing baseline backbones.

oGepteMxUI.one_liner: Iteratively refines optimization-modeling skills for coding agents via multi-level failure attribution and reverse-severity cascade evolution.
oGepteMxUI.problem: Translating natural language descriptions into valid mathematical optimization models typically relies on costly model fine-tuning or fixed agentic workflows rather than adaptable skills for general-purpose coding agents.
oGepteMxUI.method: OR-Skill runs a general-purpose agent on curated optimization tasks using a candidate skill, attributes execution failures to root causes, and aggregates them into multi-level diagnostic reports. It then applies cascade evolution in reverse order of error severity to iteratively edit and refine the reusable skill.
oGepteMxUI.key_idea: Summarize task failures into hierarchical diagnostic reports and iteratively edit an agent's optimization skill in reverse order of error severity.
oGepteMxUI.evidence: Evaluated across seven optimization modeling benchmarks including IndustryOR and ComplexLP against direct prompting, agentic workflows, skill-learning baselines, and fine-tuned models.
oGepteMxUI.claimed_gains: OR-Skill improves absolute accuracy by +21.5% on IndustryOR and +16.2% on ComplexLP.
oGepteMxUI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evolving an inspectable domain skill yields large accuracy gains over a bare agent on hard benchmarks like ComplexLP across broad baseline comparisons.
oGepteMxUI.main_concern: Reviewers raise reproducibility and evaluation validity issues, including a mathematically inconsistent length-penalized sampling score, potential sandbox answer leakage without trace audits, and unacknowledged overlap with AlphaOPT.

GRVjmvpTSi.one_liner: Evidence scope, dispersion, and reasoning depth quantify long-context question difficulty beyond context length.
GRVjmvpTSi.problem: Equal-length contexts can require very different amounts and distributions of evidence integration.
GRVjmvpTSi.method: The study defines sample-level evidence scope and dispersion and extends them with reasoning depth. LURCH pairs multi-domain questions with answers and supporting evidence to measure these properties and relate them to model failures.
GRVjmvpTSi.key_idea: Quantify how much supporting evidence a question needs, how widely it is dispersed, and how many reasoning layers connect it.
GRVjmvpTSi.evidence: Controlled experiments on proprietary and open-weight models compare evidence properties at fixed lengths and examine interactions as context length increases.
GRVjmvpTSi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation relevant and the proposed properties intuitive and supported by multi-domain experiments.
GRVjmvpTSi.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability and explanatory value of automatically derived evidence properties and the benchmark's data composition.

L6TGhhorub.one_liner: A distilled utility scorer selects the top reasoning steps for reuse according to answer improvement per verification token.
L6TGhhorub.problem: Accumulating historical reasoning steps indiscriminately can hurt performance, and apparent verification effort may not indicate usefulness.
L6TGhhorub.method: The study compares effort-based ranking with ex-post utility measured as judged-answer improvement per verification token. StepRouter distills utility into a lightweight step-text scorer that routes only the top 20% of candidate steps.
L6TGhhorub.key_idea: Rank candidate reasoning steps using learned ex-post utility and reuse only the highest-scoring subset.
L6TGhhorub.evidence: AIME and LiveCodeBench experiments cover multiple backbones, same-pool selection controls, and format-matched fine-tuning on utility-labeled examples.
L6TGhhorub.claimed_gains: StepRouter yields +19.6 pp on LiveCodeBench with DeepSeek-R1 and +23.2 pp with Qwen3-8B, reaches 97.2% on AIME with GPT-5, and 166 utility-annotated fine-tuning examples yield +12.2 pp on AIME (68.16% to 80.36%).
L6TGhhorub.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the substantial gains and same-pool controls that test step selection independently of adding context.
L6TGhhorub.main_concern: Reviewers note that scoring isolated step text without directly conditioning on the problem limits the representation of task-dependent utility.

4zBi9b2RdJ.one_liner: Temporal, spectral, and static-context views route workload states to compositions of learnable pattern experts.
4zBi9b2RdJ.problem: Historical prototype pools can generalize poorly when heterogeneous nodes experience evolving workloads.
4zBi9b2RdJ.method: SCPEC formulates multi-node forecasting as multi-view regression using temporal, spectral, and static-context state descriptions. State-conditioned routing and gated composition replace stored historical patterns with learnable pattern experts.
4zBi9b2RdJ.key_idea: Condition the selection and composition of learnable pattern experts on a node's multi-view workload state.
4zBi9b2RdJ.evidence: Experiments cover eight workload, electricity, and traffic datasets, component ablations, same-backbone MetaEformer comparisons, and ECW-derived changing-state scenarios.
4zBi9b2RdJ.claimed_gains: SCPEC achieves best or tied-best results on 15 of 16 MSE/MAE evaluation entries.
4zBi9b2RdJ.reviewer_consensus: Positive reviews value the motivation for state-conditioned pattern reuse and the empirical evidence across forecasting datasets.
4zBi9b2RdJ.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization to unseen workload patterns because changing-state evidence relies on limited scenarios from the same source dataset.

NUoT1B6r9b.one_liner: Offline performance supervision trains scorers to choose demonstration orderings before a single target-model inference.
NUoT1B6r9b.problem: Demonstration order affects in-context learning in ways that depend jointly on the query, retrieved examples, and target model.
NUoT1B6r9b.method: ADOICL learns to predict downstream performance for candidate orderings conditioned on the query, demonstrations, and target LLM. It offers a serialized sequence scorer and an embedding-first scorer that reuses representations across candidates.
NUoT1B6r9b.key_idea: Predict each candidate ordering's downstream score from offline supervision and select the best before querying the target model.
NUoT1B6r9b.evidence: Evaluations span 9 target LLMs, 5 tasks, and 8 datasets covering classification, generation, and regression, with ablations and efficiency and transfer studies.
NUoT1B6r9b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the empirical coverage across tasks and backbones is broad and the performance-oriented framing is clear.
NUoT1B6r9b.main_concern: Reviewers find the advantage over related demonstration-selection and dynamic-ordering methods unclear without direct accuracy and runtime comparisons.

HdUlQV6dde.one_liner: Anchoring final chat-template activations during benign fine-tuning preserves refusal behavior at the start of model answers.
HdUlQV6dde.problem: Harmless fine-tuning can weaken safety refusals, and existing accounts do not explain which benign datasets cause the damage.
HdUlQV6dde.method: The study tests an answer-opening account using dataset controls, prefix interventions, and activation patching. Opening Hold constrains final chat-template-token activations toward the aligned model during fine-tuning.
HdUlQV6dde.key_idea: Keep the last chat-template token's hidden activations near the aligned model's states while updating the model on benign data.
HdUlQV6dde.evidence: Experiments cover 17 models, self-generated Alpaca answers, eight additional datasets, positional interventions, and a six-model activation-anchoring evaluation.
HdUlQV6dde.claimed_gains: Holding opening activations lowers harmful compliance from 22.6% to 0.9% over six models.
HdUlQV6dde.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value investigating why benign fine-tuning weakens refusals through broad experiments and complementary interventions.
HdUlQV6dde.main_concern: Restoring refusals through prefixes or activation patches does not establish that the original harmfulness judgment remains intact.

g6cNvG8StH.one_liner: A squared-gradient-weighted stability margin connects non-monotone gradient descent to convergence through multi-step conditions.
g6cNvG8StH.problem: Classical monotone-loss analyses do not explain convergence when gradient descent operates at the Edge of Stability.
g6cNvG8StH.method: The analysis defines averaged directional sharpness along updates and a squared-gradient-weighted stability margin that exactly determines cumulative loss decrease. A sufficient condition comparing iterates several steps apart yields stationarity rates and convergence rates under the PL condition.
g6cNvG8StH.key_idea: Compare iterates several steps apart to bound a cumulative stability margin built from directional sharpness and squared gradient norms.
g6cNvG8StH.evidence: The paper verifies its condition for theoretical neural-network models and examines margin bounds in full-batch MLP and Vision Transformer experiments on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet.
g6cNvG8StH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the convergence framework as technically sound and useful for understanding non-monotone Edge-of-Stability dynamics.
g6cNvG8StH.main_concern: The guarantees rely on restricted theoretical constructions whose applicability to practical neural-network training remains unclear.

YliOpoR8bl.one_liner: Complex-covariance Gaussian splatting renders depth-dependent electron diffraction in one rasterization pass.
YliOpoR8bl.problem: Ray-based tomographic Gaussian splatting discards scattering depth and becomes inaccurate in sufficiently high-resolution imaging.
YliOpoR8bl.method: CryoWaveGS uses a wave-optical forward model in which Fresnel propagation transforms Gaussians into Gaussians with complex covariance. This formulation renders depth-resolved diffraction in a single pass.
YliOpoR8bl.key_idea: Encode depth-dependent Fresnel propagation in complex Gaussian covariances and render the resulting diffraction through Gaussian rasterization.
YliOpoR8bl.evidence: Independent multislice simulations validate the renderer, and measured cryo-ET and atomic-resolution tilt series compare it with conventional, implicit-field, and matched ray-based baselines.
YliOpoR8bl.claimed_gains: End-to-end cost stays within 1.3× that of the ray-based renderer on the densest run.
YliOpoR8bl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the physically motivated complex-covariance formulation and its controlled forward-model validation.
YliOpoR8bl.main_concern: The experiments provide limited independent evidence that the wave-optical contribution improves practical high-resolution 3D reconstruction.

F8rhzu26eT.one_liner: Stationary state-space covariance shapes diffusion noise into causal temporal correlations for spatiotemporal prediction.
F8rhzu26eT.problem: Independent framewise diffusion noise leaves temporal structure entirely to the denoiser, while zero-state temporal filtering under-noises early frames.
F8rhzu26eT.method: DSSD learns damped oscillatory modes of a stable diagonal state-space model and uses the Cholesky factor of its stationary covariance for temporal mixing. The denoiser predicts correlated noise, and sampling removes and reapplies the mixing.
F8rhzu26eT.key_idea: Apply the Cholesky factor of learned stationary state-space covariance to noise, preserving per-frame variance while introducing causal temporal correlations.
F8rhzu26eT.evidence: The paper proves causality, invertibility, variance preservation, and Kalman-innovations equivalence, and compares shared-denoiser baselines on scientific-field and robot-video datasets.
F8rhzu26eT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the temporal-corruption framework and empirical improvements across multiple prediction tasks.
F8rhzu26eT.main_concern: Comparisons omit strong forecasting and diffusion baselines, limiting evidence of competitiveness beyond matched-denoiser controls.

IMAYVonoLA.one_liner: Exchange-isolated attention and a hierarchy loss remove historical-answer shortcuts during hierarchical visual instruction tuning.
IMAYVonoLA.problem: Preceding ground-truth taxonomic answers can let vision-language models solve hierarchical recognition tasks without sufficient visual evidence.
IMAYVonoLA.method: The framework masks dependencies on earlier question-answer exchanges while retaining shared visual information through Exchange-Isolated Causal Attention. A probabilistic hierarchy loss encourages consistency across semantic levels.
IMAYVonoLA.key_idea: Block attention to preceding question-answer exchanges while sharing visual inputs and explicitly penalizing taxonomically inconsistent predictions.
IMAYVonoLA.evidence: Reference-taxonomy analysis and controlled interventions diagnose shortcuts, and three generative VLM backbones undergo seen, unseen, and cross-domain evaluation on iNat21-Plant and iNat21-Animal.
IMAYVonoLA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the simple framework and reported empirical improvements over the selected baselines.
IMAYVonoLA.main_concern: Experimental support remains limited, particularly beyond biology and against closely related hierarchical training methods.

FBSpbYyrGE.one_liner: Behavioral steering directions become visual fingerprints for black-box verification of vision-language model provenance.
FBSpbYyrGE.problem: Output-trigger fingerprints lack an explicit connection to inherited internal features that explains their persistence across model derivation.
FBSpbYyrGE.method: SteerPrint formalizes persistent, distinguishing internal features as provenance anchors. It selects behavioral directions in representation space and distills their effects into visual inputs whose generated responses support ownership verification.
FBSpbYyrGE.key_idea: Distill the behavioral effects of inherited representation-space steering directions into visual triggers detectable through generated text.
FBSpbYyrGE.evidence: Experiments cover recent LVLMs, downstream fine-tuning, quantization, pruning, and model merging.
FBSpbYyrGE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value ownership verification through generated outputs without modifying released weights or accessing suspect-model internals.
FBSpbYyrGE.main_concern: Missing baselines and mismatched evaluation protocols weaken the evidence for verification performance and specificity.

hS02qE5NLR.one_liner: Compresses target-model features into shared latent queries before drafting an entire speculative token block in parallel.
hS02qE5NLR.problem: Parallel speculative drafters lack an explicit shared future representation for coordinating candidate tokens and extending accepted prefixes.
hS02qE5NLR.method: LatentSpec's Thinker updates a small set of latent queries from intermediate frozen-target features. Its Drafter conditions on this shared state to predict the whole candidate block in parallel for standard speculative verification.
hS02qE5NLR.key_idea: Concentrate part of drafting computation in a few shared latent positions that condition all parallel candidate tokens.
hS02qE5NLR.evidence: Experiments with Qwen3 models compare DFlash variants across benchmarks, measuring acceptance length, draft latency, FLOPs, and end-to-end throughput.
hS02qE5NLR.claimed_gains: Relative to DFlash, LatentSpec reduces drafting FLOPs by 8.26–9.41% and increases end-to-end throughput by up to 9.33% while preserving or improving average acceptance length.
hS02qE5NLR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the latent computation allocation sensible and appreciate reporting practical latency and throughput alongside acceptance length.
hS02qE5NLR.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate whether gains come from shared latent reasoning or a generic change in capacity and compute allocation.

AXfkYvNftW.one_liner: Derives boundary and transition-representation costs for Lipschitz repair of fixed hard-routed mixture-of-experts functions.
AXfkYvNftW.problem: Making neighboring experts agree at routing boundaries does not ensure that a sparse repair can represent transitions back to original outputs.
AXfkYvNftW.method: The paper studies squared-distortion-minimizing Lipschitz repair while preserving selected expert sets. Boundary-layer inequalities yield shallow-width obstructions, while constructive repairs and low-dimensional oracles establish attainable costs.
AXfkYvNftW.key_idea: Relate approximation error in boundary transition layers to excess Lipschitz-repair risk while keeping expert selection fixed.
AXfkYvNftW.evidence: Theoretical depth and width bounds accompany numerical repair comparisons, frozen Switch Transformer boundary measurements, and selected-set-preserving layer repair comparisons.
AXfkYvNftW.claimed_gains: A two-stage repair evaluates two ReLUs per input for relative risk 1+O(L^{-2}), whereas shallow ReLU branches need width \Omega(L^{2/5}) to match this order.
AXfkYvNftW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical separation between boundary agreement and transition representation, including its quantitative architectural costs.
AXfkYvNftW.main_concern: Restrictive fixed-function and shallow-branch assumptions leave the implications for practical trained mixture-of-experts systems unclear.

WajrFynqDU.one_liner: Matches cached CLIP images in a text-induced subspace and retrieves local patches through class-competitive comparisons.
WajrFynqDU.problem: Cache membership based on image-text predictions can conflict with full-space image-image retrieval, while pooled features miss localized class evidence.
WajrFynqDU.method: DCM preserves the underlying adapter's pseudo-labeling and cache updates but projects global matching into a fixed text-induced subspace. It also reuses retained images' ViT patch tokens for fine-grained, class-competitive patch retrieval.
WajrFynqDU.key_idea: Align global cache similarity with text-defined class directions and supplement it with cross-class competitive patch matching.
WajrFynqDU.evidence: Cross-dataset and out-of-distribution experiments span multiple cache adapters and CLIP backbones, alongside conditional margin analysis and ablations.
WajrFynqDU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate treating cache retrieval separately from construction while preserving existing adapter update rules.
WajrFynqDU.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the contribution of class competition and class-conditioned query-patch selection within the local branch.

gGhcZq5Jy7.one_liner: Reweights preference pairs using conformal nonconformity scores and structural-risk calibration to reduce harmful updates from noisy labels.
gGhcZq5Jy7.problem: Flipped preference labels invert DPO gradients, and model-internal uncertainty heuristics can fail to identify corrupted pairs.
gGhcZq5Jy7.method: CPW combines split-conformal preference p-values with a quantile bound on pair-level structural risk. CPW+ fuses multiple views and selects a threshold with Learn-then-Test control and a Hoeffding-Bentkus certificate under a model-based extractor.
gGhcZq5Jy7.key_idea: Down-weight preference pairs using calibrated nonconformity and relational structural-risk signals rather than model-internal uncertainty alone.
gGhcZq5Jy7.evidence: Experiments use multiple model families and real human- and AI-annotated preference datasets, with matched seeds, weight-shuffle controls, and a separate corrected certification analysis.
gGhcZq5Jy7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the weight-shuffle controls showing that which pairs receive lower weights matters beyond overall update scaling.
gGhcZq5Jy7.main_concern: The guarantee controls structural risk rather than label correctness, and the main experiments use an earlier uncertified calibration rule.

mS7J36xbKx.one_liner: Pulls endpoint forces through a denoiser Jacobian and scales atom-wise updates to guide frozen crystal diffusion models.
mS7J36xbKx.problem: Physical guidance must reconcile endpoint forces with current diffusion coordinates and unequal atomic response scales in periodic crystals.
mS7J36xbKx.method: CrystalJTF applies the predicted clean endpoint map's Jacobian transpose to endpoint forces. Relative-BB adapts atom-wise scales from sampling history, and a periodic geometry cap limits displacements while generator, potential, lattice sampling, and element sampling remain fixed.
mS7J36xbKx.key_idea: Backpropagate endpoint forces to current coordinates, then apply history-adaptive atom-wise scaling and a periodic displacement cap.
mS7J36xbKx.evidence: Six settings across CrysLLM-Gen, DiffCSP, and MatterGen evaluate composition-conditioned and unconditional generation with SUN/MSUN metrics.
mS7J36xbKx.claimed_gains: The abstract reports average SUN and MSUN increases of 1.28 and 4.78 under CHGNet 0.3.0, but truncates the percentage-unit specification.
mS7J36xbKx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a training-free plug-in that improves stability-related metrics across different frozen crystal generators.
mS7J36xbKx.main_concern: Missing tuned simpler guidance baselines leave the necessity of atom-adaptive scaling, geometry caps, and fixed controller choices uncertain.

8IgcgVlgVc.one_liner: Trains concept-conditioned low-rank attention-projection adaptations on pooled preferences for context-dependent steering of unseen concepts.
8IgcgVlgVc.problem: Fixed linear activation steering can bottleneck multiple behavioral distinctions and fail to adapt interventions to context.
8IgcgVlgVc.method: MetaSteer applies low-rank adaptations to attention projection matrices and trains them with preference-based optimization on pooled concept supervision. A single trained intervention transfers to unseen concepts and out-of-distribution contexts.
8IgcgVlgVc.key_idea: Condition attention-projection adaptations on concept-bearing prompts so their induced activation changes depend on the input context.
8IgcgVlgVc.evidence: Evaluation spans six backbones, three text-generation benchmarks, and three agentic settings, with hidden-trajectory analyses and capability-retention checks.
8IgcgVlgVc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad evaluation of one concept-conditioned intervention across unseen concepts, model families, and agentic tasks.
8IgcgVlgVc.main_concern: Missing matched controls leave the method insufficiently distinguished from ordinary concept-conditioned LoRA-DPO fine-tuning and prompt instruction effects.

1oxXmuogPk.one_liner: Combines support-mask geometry with organ and peripheral-background prototypes for cross-domain few-shot medical segmentation.
1oxXmuogPk.problem: Medical imaging domain shifts undermine appearance-based few-shot segmentation features, while graph-matching alternatives can be computationally expensive.
1oxXmuogPk.method: GPS modulates feature responses with geometric shape priors and mines multiple prototypes for target organs and surrounding tissues. A prototype refinement module combines this support information for cross-domain segmentation.
1oxXmuogPk.key_idea: Use support geometry and separate organ/peripheral-tissue prototypes as anatomical references under imaging domain shifts.
1oxXmuogPk.evidence: Reviewers describe abdominal and cardiac evaluations across modalities, cross-institution testing, external datasets, and shared-backbone baseline comparisons.
1oxXmuogPk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find combining anatomical geometry with peripheral context reasonable and acknowledge broad segmentation evaluation.
1oxXmuogPk.main_concern: The protocol does not clearly establish disjoint source and target classes, annotation provenance, or patient partitions for the claimed few-shot setting.

gh5lYUmCs7.one_liner: Routes reliability-selected local evidence and view-rejection context into adaptive prompts for aerial-ground person re-identification.
gh5lYUmCs7.problem: Drone and ground viewpoints make local pedestrian cues unevenly reliable because visibility, scale, and surrounding context change.
gh5lYUmCs7.method: RAPR initializes prompts from shared and input-conditioned sources and selects local evidence consistent with a view-reduced identity anchor. A refiner separates identity relevance from view bias to calibrate local memory and bidirectional prompt-local interactions before global-local descriptor fusion.
gh5lYUmCs7.key_idea: Use identity-anchor consistency and view-bias estimates to select prompt-update evidence and calibrate local feature aggregation.
gh5lYUmCs7.evidence: Experiments and component studies cover several aerial-ground re-identification benchmarks and protocols, including controlled ViT comparisons on CARGO.
gh5lYUmCs7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reliability-aware evidence selection and subsequent local refinement coherent responses to viewpoint-dependent cue quality.
gh5lYUmCs7.main_concern: Reviewers question the methodological advance beyond existing view decoupling, adaptive prompts, and bidirectional local refinement.

StHR9GSc6i.one_liner: Allocates simulation budget across shared and split SDE path segments to improve terminal-distribution estimates.
StHR9GSc6i.problem: Independent SDE sampling may waste simulation budget, but sharing partial trajectories introduces dependence that complicates distribution estimation.
StHR9GSc6i.method: The method constructs trees of partial SDE paths and analyzes their dependent empirical distributions. Asymptotic covariance and error characterizations motivate learned splitting allocations for terminal-law estimation.
StHR9GSc6i.key_idea: Share early trajectory segments and allocate branching according to their contributions to terminal-distribution estimation error.
StHR9GSc6i.evidence: Covariance formulas, limit theorems, and allocation guarantees accompany SDE and diffusion-model experiments measuring KS distance, MMD, decision regret, and tail-risk error.
StHR9GSc6i.claimed_gains: At equal compute, learned splitting reduces mean KS distance by 12–26%, MMD by 17–26%, decision regret by 28–65%, and tail-risk RMSE by 35–57%.
StHR9GSc6i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of estimating terminal distributions under a fixed budget and explicitly accounting for dependence from shared paths.
StHR9GSc6i.main_concern: Learned allocation does not consistently outperform simpler fixed or scalar-parameter splitting strategies.

3appZGYsMg.one_liner: Suppresses dominant visual-key directions in attention scores to restore query-dependent region selection and reduce object hallucination.
3appZGYsMg.problem: Vision-language models can attend heavily to images yet hallucinate because visual attention selects similar regions regardless of the generated word.
3appZGYsMg.method: The paper links concentrated visual-key directions to weak query-dependent selection and introduces training-free Whitened Attention Steering. It suppresses dominant directions in visual scores with the stated aim of maintaining image-attention allocation.
3appZGYsMg.key_idea: Whiten dominant visual attention-score directions so different text queries can rank image regions differently.
3appZGYsMg.evidence: Analyses and steering controls examine LLaVA-1.5, InstructBLIP, and Qwen3-VL, including reversed interventions and corrections along alternative directions or heads.
3appZGYsMg.claimed_gains: On LLaVA-1.5, the share of captions containing a hallucinated object falls from 54% to 30%.
3appZGYsMg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing visual attention allocation from region selection and acknowledge effective hallucination-reducing interventions.
3appZGYsMg.main_concern: Matching visual-logit moments does not exactly preserve joint-softmax attention mass, so improved selection is not isolated from changed image-attention allocation.

9E1uuL9NBp.one_liner: Runs exact facility-location greedy selection in a persistent GPU kernel with memory-aware tiling and certified multi-token admissions.
9E1uuL9NBp.problem: Serial lazy-greedy solvers and repeated GPU marginal-gain recomputation make facility-location token selection slow.
9E1uuL9NBp.method: Flash Greedy tiles the similarity matrix across streaming multiprocessors and storage tiers while retaining private coverage vectors in a persistent CUDA kernel. Boolean support checks certify unchanged gains, allowing multiple candidates per iteration without changing the naive-greedy solution.
9E1uuL9NBp.key_idea: Keep coverage and tiled similarities resident, then certify exact candidate gains with Boolean support checks to admit multiple greedy selections.
9E1uuL9NBp.evidence: Exactness proofs and placement-specific IO analysis accompany A100 latency experiments using similarity matrices from MMTok, SCOPE, and Selective Annotation.
9E1uuL9NBp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial kernel-level acceleration while preserving the exact greedy selection result.
9E1uuL9NBp.main_concern: Comparisons against original PyTorch loops lack an optimized fused GPU baseline to isolate gains beyond kernel fusion and implementation quality.

YM0ErJt9Ij.one_liner: Filters viral proteins from ESM-2 pretraining and measures selective degradation and recovery through subsequent fine-tuning.
YM0ErJt9Ij.problem: The effectiveness and durability of pretraining-data filtering as a protein-model safeguard remain uncertain across model scales.
YM0ErJt9Ij.method: The study trains ESM-2 variants with viral-protein filtering and evaluates viral and non-viral prediction performance. It then fine-tunes on removed viral families to measure recovery and computational cost.
YM0ErJt9Ij.key_idea: Compare filtered and unfiltered pretraining across model sizes, then reintroduce removed-family sequences through fine-tuning to test durability.
YM0ErJt9Ij.evidence: ESM-2 models from 8M to 3B parameters undergo masked-language-modeling, mutation-effect, and long-range contact evaluations across filtering strategies and viral families.
YM0ErJt9Ij.claimed_gains: Fine-tuning restores lost performance even for the largest models at about 80 USD of H100 time.
YM0ErJt9Ij.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the filtering study across model sizes and the concrete recovery analysis testing safeguard durability.
YM0ErJt9Ij.main_concern: Changes in protein-prediction metrics do not establish corresponding changes in biological misuse capability or practical safety.

ZOHNMriZYv.one_liner: Screens normalized label signals and coordinates shared randomness to reduce sample costs for pointwise replicable learning.
ZOHNMriZYv.problem: Models trained on independent samples can disagree at a fixed test point despite similar risks, creating sample and shared-randomness tradeoffs.
ZOHNMriZYv.method: The paper uses normalized label-signal screening on countable domains and central voting for realizable learning. Risk-weighted nested thresholds handle arbitrary domains, with separate analyses of finite shared seeds, structured classes, and properness constraints.
ZOHNMriZYv.key_idea: Screen normalized label signals and coordinate prediction decisions with shared randomized thresholds or central voting.
ZOHNMriZYv.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds cover agnostic and realizable learning, countable and arbitrary domains, and joint sample-randomness tradeoffs.
ZOHNMriZYv.claimed_gains: On countable domains, the agnostic sample bound becomes \widetilde O(d/(\rho^2\alpha^2)) without the previous additive overhead, while central voting achieves \widetilde O(d/(\rho^2\alpha)) in the realizable case.
ZOHNMriZYv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial theoretical progress on sample complexity and shared-randomness tradeoffs for pointwise replicability.
ZOHNMriZYv.main_concern: All reviewers find the dense exposition and insufficiently introduced notation difficult to follow.

vr07uUzn1K.one_liner: Reads point tracks from frozen video diffusion attention using confidence-weighted heads, bilinear source sampling, and local position decoding.
vr07uUzn1K.problem: Frozen video diffusion features support correspondence estimation, but readout choices can limit point-tracking accuracy.
vr07uUzn1K.method: The readout combines confidence-weighted attention heads, bilinear query sampling, local sub-token decoding, and visibility estimation from one transformer block. Settings selected on labeled synthetic clips transfer unchanged to real videos without training a tracking network.
vr07uUzn1K.key_idea: Combine bilinearly sampled source descriptors with local attention-based sub-token decoding and confidence-weighted head aggregation.
vr07uUzn1K.evidence: Evaluation uses 20 labeled synthetic selection clips, TAP-Vid DAVIS and Kinetics, matched released-HeFT comparisons, and six checkpoints from three generator families.
vr07uUzn1K.claimed_gains: CogVideoX-2B reaches 5.21 AJ on TAP-Vid DAVIS and 44.00 on Kinetics, with Kinetics gains of +18.62 and +12.77 AJ over matched HeFT for CogVideoX and Wan.
vr07uUzn1K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the matched HeFT comparisons and controlled empirical analysis of a training-free tracking readout.
vr07uUzn1K.main_concern: The components largely reuse established feature matching and sub-token decoding, making the contribution primarily an empirical integration and analysis.

pkymKR1YiW.one_liner: Moves rules relative to facts and causally probes token positions to explain failures to use still-accessible information.
pkymKR1YiW.problem: Direct-answer language models may ignore a relevant fact when its governing rule appears later, despite retaining knowledge of the fact.
pkymKR1YiW.method: The study moves one unchanged rule while holding facts fixed and tests whether the answer uses the named fact. Causal experiments examine where rule outcomes form and which token positions the final verdict reads.
pkymKR1YiW.key_idea: Compare rule-before-fact and rule-after-fact layouts, then intervene on fact-position representations to trace where rule outcomes enter the answer.
pkymKR1YiW.evidence: Controlled experiments cover 18 open models, closed-model comparisons, prompt variations, established rule-application benchmarks, and causal representation interventions.
pkymKR1YiW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled single-sentence manipulation and systematic separation of knowing a fact from using it.
pkymKR1YiW.main_concern: Synthetic direct-answer tasks provide limited evidence that the same failure and remedy generalize to deployed guardrails, judges, or complex policies.

osEETKbSYB.one_liner: Uses pessimistic reliability estimates to route queries between language models and capacity-limited experts while accounting for queues.
osEETKbSYB.problem: Deferral must balance answer reliability and congestion while learning from selectively observed expert labels delayed by queuing.
osEETKbSYB.method: KL-PBD maintains Kullback-Leibler lower confidence bounds for accuracy at each confidence level and uses these pessimistic estimates to guide deferral. Its analysis accounts for how learning changes the queue-dependent decision threshold.
osEETKbSYB.key_idea: Insert lower confidence bounds on model reliability into congestion-aware deferral decisions while updating estimates from delayed expert feedback.
osEETKbSYB.evidence: Matching regret bounds accompany synthetic experiments and offline question-answering replays using GSM8K, NuminaMath, and MedMCQA.
osEETKbSYB.claimed_gains: KL-PBD achieves O(K\log T) gap-dependent regret away from the deferral boundary and \widetilde{O}(\sqrt{KT}) worst-case regret, matching lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.
osEETKbSYB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the detailed regret analysis and the justification for pessimistic decisions under selective feedback and congestion.
osEETKbSYB.main_concern: Learning independent confidence bins from scratch without prior calibration or query context makes the modeled online setting potentially unrealistic and sample-inefficient.

D4v70Ms5WW.one_liner: Trains a unified LLM router via decoupled mode-and-execution GRPO advantages and progressive exploration across routing paradigms.
D4v70Ms5WW.problem: Existing LLM routers lock queries into a single predefined execution structure—single-round, multi-round, or agentic—limiting adaptation to varying query complexity.
D4v70Ms5WW.method: RouteWeaver integrates single-round, multi-round, and agentic model coordination inside a single LLM router policy using a shared action grammar. It trains this policy with COMET-GRPO, which decouples trajectory-level advantages into separate credit signals for mode selection and within-mode worker execution, paired with progressive exploration that anneals from externally assigned modes to autonomous mode choice.
D4v70Ms5WW.key_idea: Unify single-round, multi-round, and agentic LLM routing in one policy trained via decoupled mode/execution GRPO credit assignment and annealed mode exploration.
D4v70Ms5WW.evidence: Evaluated with a Qwen3-4B router coordinating six worker LLMs across five domains—mathematics, coding, knowledge, logical reasoning, and factual recall (including held-out AIME, GPQA-D, and BBH).
D4v70Ms5WW.claimed_gains: Achieves an average accuracy of 61.4%, an 11.03% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, while outperforming all compared baselines in each of the five domains.
D4v70Ms5WW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying execution-mode selection and worker coordination in a single action grammar with progressive exploration is well motivated and delivers strong cross-domain accuracy.
D4v70Ms5WW.main_concern: Reviewers note missing fixed-mode router baselines using the same worker pool and grammar, multi-candidate code scoring that deviates from strict pass@1, and cost accounting that omits the Qwen3-4B router's own inference overhead.

FLzUMEqJr5.one_liner: Steers middle-layer LLM activations to independently manipulate and compose function semantics, programming language, and implementation strategy.
FLzUMEqJr5.problem: Whether code-generating LLMs rely on language-specific surface patterns or reusable, factored internal representations shared across programming languages and strategies remains unclear.
FLzUMEqJr5.method: The authors apply leave-one-context-out activation steering to middle-layer LLM hidden states during code generation to independently intervene on target function, programming language, and implementation strategy, including composing function and language edits on underspecified prompts. They complement these interventions with cross-language fine-tuning transfer tests on arbitrary functions and a synthetic minimal transformer model with an exact Bayesian reference.
FLzUMEqJr5.key_idea: Extract and compose out-of-context middle-layer activation steering vectors for function identity, programming language, and implementation strategy during LLM code generation.
FLzUMEqJr5.evidence: Evaluated via execution-verified activation steering across 4 digit-arithmetic functions, 10 programming languages, and strategy pairs on screened LLMs plus RWKV, cross-language fine-tuning transfer, and a synthetic transformer toy model.
FLzUMEqJr5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that estimating function and language steering vectors out-of-context and composing them on underspecified prompts with execution-based checks provides clean causal evidence of reusable representations.
FLzUMEqJr5.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical evidence is restricted to four simple arithmetic functions and models pre-screened for suffix addressability (failing on Mistral-Small), and cannot rule out compressed task-summary states.

CGzXLWNbkP.one_liner: Weights step-level RL baselines by preceding-action similarity and applies difficulty-calibrated echo-loop penalties for multi-turn LLM agents.
CGzXLWNbkP.problem: Stepwise group-relative RL for multi-turn LLM agents groups states solely by current observations, suffering from observation aliasing across distinct action histories and unpenalized repetitive action loops.
CGzXLWNbkP.method: Action Echo Policy Optimization (AEPO) extends critic-free group-relative RL with two mechanisms: Action-Conditioned Spatial Disambiguation (ACSD), which builds a soft-weighted step baseline using preceding-action text similarity to reduce observation aliasing, and Difficulty-Aware Echo Regularization (DAER), which applies a dynamically calibrated trajectory penalty on delayed or redundant state arrivals.
CGzXLWNbkP.key_idea: Combine soft step-level baseline weighting by preceding-action text similarity with a difficulty-calibrated trajectory arrival-delay penalty in critic-free multi-turn agent RL.
CGzXLWNbkP.evidence: Evaluated across two model scales and three seeds on ALFWorld and WebShop against GRPO, GiGPO, RAGEN (StarPO-S), and ProxMO alongside component ablations.
CGzXLWNbkP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that AEPO reuses existing rollouts without a learned critic or extra branching to address observation aliasing and repetitive loops, achieving consistent gains on ALFWorld and WebShop.
CGzXLWNbkP.main_concern: Reviewers point out that single-step lexical (TF-IDF) action similarity may miss multi-step history dependencies or semantic equivalence, while DAER's action-agnostic state keys can penalize valid exploration.

KYP59dCEzn.one_liner: Organizes LLM agent context into nested intents with recursive prefix consolidation and hierarchical detail recovery.
KYP59dCEzn.problem: Long-running LLM agents struggle to convert continuous interaction streams into reusable knowledge without overflowing active context or losing recoverable episodic details during summarization.
KYP59dCEzn.method: Hippocam structures ongoing agent execution as nested intents—consolidating completed sub-intents into task-relevant outcomes—while recursively consolidating older history prefixes into progressively more abstract summaries that retain links to raw interactions for top-down detail recovery. Recalled past memories re-enter active intent contexts and undergo re-consolidation alongside new experiences without parameter updates.
KYP59dCEzn.key_idea: Structure active agent context as nested intents paired with recursive prefix abstraction, hierarchical raw-trace recovery, and re-consolidation of recalled memories upon reuse.
KYP59dCEzn.evidence: Evaluated on continual learning, cross-domain transfer, conflicting information updates, and long-horizon agent benchmarks (including ALFWorld) with component and memory-transition analyses.
KYP59dCEzn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying active intent-boundary management, recursive historical abstraction, and progressive raw-detail recovery offers a coherent, parameter-free memory architecture for long-running agents.
KYP59dCEzn.main_concern: Reviewers note unmatched inference compute, reasoning, and tool budgets across baselines (with flat summaries matching 100% on ALFWorld) and weak quantitative evidence for the claimed disuse-fading effect.

zuWoqgGiXt.one_liner: Maintains factored variable distributions inside particles and ranks LLM-synthesized world-model programs by filtering likelihood.
zuWoqgGiXt.problem: Concrete particle filters in partially observed code world models commit every hidden variable to a single value per particle, exhausting fixed particle budgets as joint hidden-state assignments grow combinatorially.
zuWoqgGiXt.method: The paper introduces distributional particles (d-particles) whose individual state variables hold distributions over possible values, paired with Abstract Belief Coder (ABC). ABC uses a shared Factor Library to propagate and condition variable distributions and compute filtering likelihoods, while an LLM proposes state representations and world-model programs ranked by this filtering likelihood.
zuWoqgGiXt.key_idea: Represent each particle's hidden variables as parametric distributions updated via a shared Factor Library, and select LLM-generated world-model programs using particle-filtering likelihood.
zuWoqgGiXt.evidence: Evaluated on six partially observed MiniGrid tasks and two customized Crafter tasks using both ground-truth and LLM-generated world models against concrete-particle baselines.
zuWoqgGiXt.claimed_gains: On six partially observed MiniGrid tasks, ABC achieves 90.6% success versus 55.0% for a concrete-particle baseline with ground-truth models, and 75.6% versus 46.1% with LLM-generated models.
zuWoqgGiXt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining distributional Rao-Blackwellized particles with LLM-generated world-model programs and a shared distribution library is a well-motivated approach to scaling belief tracking over multiple hidden variables.
zuWoqgGiXt.main_concern: Experiments are restricted to small, controlled grid-world tasks with factored per-particle independence assumptions that leave approximation errors and scalability under strongly coupled or complex dynamics untested.

ogkbzMk5Yr.one_liner: Constructs a multi-view 3D intraoral scan VQA benchmark spanning arch, tooth, and surface dental caries reasoning.
ogkbzMk5Yr.problem: Existing dental vision-language benchmarks focus on image-level recognition rather than jointly evaluating hierarchical arch-to-tooth-to-surface reasoning, cross-view evidence integration, and surface-level caries assessment.
ogkbzMk5Yr.method: CariesBench compiles 5,932 3D intraoral scans into 85,455 standardized multi-view renderings and 133,994 expert-checked VQA instances organized across Arch-level Clinical Screening (ACS), Tooth-level Diagnostic Reasoning (TDR), and Structured Clinical Decision-Making (SCD). The authors also fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on the CariesBench training split to produce IntraoralGPT.
ogkbzMk5Yr.key_idea: Render standardized multi-view images from 3D intraoral scans to evaluate arch-level screening, tooth-level diagnosis, and surface-level clinical decision-making jointly.
ogkbzMk5Yr.evidence: Benchmarks 24 baseline multimodal large language models alongside the fine-tuned IntraoralGPT model across patient-level data splits on 133,994 VQA instances.
ogkbzMk5Yr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large-scale, patient-split dataset and its clinically structured progression from arch-level screening to tooth- and surface-level assessment across 24 evaluated MLLMs.
ogkbzMk5Yr.main_concern: The evaluation lacks controlled single-view versus multi-view ablations to verify cross-view integration, alongside label-distribution inconsistencies in the Sound Tooth Verification subtask.

rmC1KQxmMH.one_liner: Builds noise-model-free multi-objective Bayesian optimization acquisitions via soft non-dominance indicators and observation subsampling.
rmC1KQxmMH.problem: Input-dependent heteroscedastic observation noise corrupts Pareto dominance relations in multi-objective Bayesian optimization and cannot generally be identified from single evaluations per design.
rmC1KQxmMH.method: The paper constructs likelihood-free versions of two hypervolume-based acquisition functions using a soft non-dominance indicator and subsampling-based utilities learned directly from noisy observations without an explicit noise model. It also derives an exact loss decomposition into sampling, set-selection, and mis-selection terms alongside dominance-preservation and Pareto-alignment guarantees.
rmC1KQxmMH.key_idea: Construct likelihood-free hypervolume acquisition functions directly from noisy observations using a subsampling-based soft non-dominance indicator without specifying an explicit noise model.
rmC1KQxmMH.evidence: Supported by dominance-preservation and Pareto-alignment proofs for classes of homoscedastic and heteroscedastic noise, an exact decision-maker loss decomposition showing mis-selection exceeds 40% of loss at high noise, and empirical comparisons against GP-based baselines.
rmC1KQxmMH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the computationally tractable likelihood-free acquisition formulation that avoids explicit heteroscedastic noise modeling on noisy multi-objective black-box problems.
