rmC1KQxmMH.main_concern: Reviewers question whether subsampling mitigates false positives from extreme positive noise, note that Pareto-alignment guarantees may not cover the motivating heteroscedastic setting, and point out missing baselines such as PESMO/JESMO and qPOTS.

utT3Mpf4S5.one_liner: Trains a compact state-ranking policy directly against compiled relaxed decision diagram dual bounds without solved instances or value targets.
utT3Mpf4S5.problem: Imitating backward cost-to-go values from wider relaxed decision diagrams introduces systematic optimism bias for state ranking, and even exact cost-to-go targets underperform under width caps.
utT3Mpf4S5.method: For the traveling salesman problem with a drone, the authors discard intermediate value targets and directly optimize a 22-parameter state-ranking policy against the certified dual bound produced by compiling the relaxed decision diagram. Because compilation preserves bound validity under any ranking rule, training needs no solved instances.
utT3Mpf4S5.key_idea: Optimize the width-capped state-merging ranking policy directly against the compiled relaxed decision diagram's certified lower bound rather than fitting biased or exact cost-to-go targets.
utT3Mpf4S5.evidence: Analysis of relaxation-target optimism bias and evaluations on traveling salesman problem with a drone benchmarks across problem sizes against relaxed-target imitation, exact-target imitation, and hand-designed f+h ranking.
utT3Mpf4S5.claimed_gains: Optimizing a 22-parameter policy directly on the bound beats exact-target imitation by 1.88 and 3.27 gap points, beats relaxed-target imitation by 4.4–5.8 points, and improves over the hand-designed f+h rule by 6.1–8.8 points on at least 99 of 100 test instances per configuration.
utT3Mpf4S5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate diagnosing systematic optimism bias in relaxed cost-to-go supervision and showing unsupervised bound-direct training consistently tightens certified lower bounds on unseen instances.
utT3Mpf4S5.main_concern: Reviewers note it is unclear how a bucket-constant learned term alters state retention without an explicit cross-bucket width-allocation explanation, and advantages narrow on larger instances under matched compute.

c7ef6zwJgk.one_liner: Evaluates vision-language models across perception, target identification, and toxicity classification on 14,940 human-annotated toxic and benign visual illusions.
c7ef6zwJgk.problem: End-to-end moderation benchmarks for AI-generated visual illusions lack non-toxic and failed-illusion controls, making it hard to localize errors across perception, target recognition, and toxicity judgment.
c7ef6zwJgk.method: ToxicIllusion introduces a human-annotated benchmark of 14,940 images generated from 166 toxic and non-toxic targets spanning English text, Chinese text, gestures, and symbols, including non-illusion cases. A three-stage diagnostic framework evaluates illusion perception, exact target identification, and toxicity classification alongside representation and spatial relevance-map analyses.
c7ef6zwJgk.key_idea: Decompose visual-illusion moderation into illusion perception, exact target identification, and toxicity classification across matched toxic, non-toxic, and non-illusion controls to localize VLM bottlenecks.
c7ef6zwJgk.evidence: Evaluated across vision-language models (eight API and open-weight models per reviews) on 14,940 human-annotated images across 166 targets and four target types, with conditional toxicity and representation analyses.
c7ef6zwJgk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the three-stage diagnostic evaluation and inclusion of non-toxic and failed-illusion controls across 14,940 annotated images.
c7ef6zwJgk.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing prior hidden-content VLM benchmarks (SemVink/HC-Bench, where image downscaling solves recognition), lack of independent human target-naming verification, and strict exact-match or visibility-gating confounds.

FlXYRIcA3P.one_liner: Consolidates experience into symbolic knowledge and compiles it into neural memory across interchangeable embodied-agent components.
FlXYRIcA3P.problem: Neurosymbolic embodied agents couple reasoning and lifelong learning to specific foundation models, symbolic tools, and knowledge formats.
FlXYRIcA3P.method: NeSyChain connects components through a shared knowledge layer and applies two-stage learning: contrastive validation consolidates acquired data into symbolic knowledge, which is then compiled into neural memory on a frozen model. The modular structure remains fixed across configurations.
FlXYRIcA3P.key_idea: Route component interactions through a shared knowledge layer and transform experience first into validated symbols and then into reusable neural memory.
FlXYRIcA3P.evidence: Experiments span 6 neurosymbolic configurations, 4 foundation models, 9 symbolic tools, 3 knowledge formats, 3 benchmarks, and real-world settings.
FlXYRIcA3P.claimed_gains: NeSyChain reports 21.8% higher task success than the strongest baseline on every benchmark.
FlXYRIcA3P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating symbolic consolidation from neural compilation is well motivated and that evaluation across configurations, benchmarks, and real robots is broad.
FlXYRIcA3P.main_concern: Reviewers question algorithmic novelty beyond integrating prior consolidation and compilation methods and whether standardized interfaces ensure semantic interchangeability.

xaMzfArgut.one_liner: Extends alignment elasticity with dataset and representation dimensions to explain fine-tuning-induced alignment rebound.
xaMzfArgut.problem: Equally sized pretraining and alignment datasets can produce different resistance to alignment rebound, which dataset-scale elasticity theory does not explain.
xaMzfArgut.method: Alleviation Elasticity Theory introduces alignment-data dimension and internal model-representation dimension as measures of abstract and absorbed information. Entropy incorporates both into joint-distribution weights intended to characterize drift toward the pretraining distribution after fine-tuning.
xaMzfArgut.key_idea: Weight data contributions by entropy-linked dataset intrinsic dimension and model-perceived representation dimension when estimating alignment elasticity.
xaMzfArgut.evidence: The theory develops effective-data-volume and elasticity expressions, with preliminary experiments using DistilGPT2 on IMDb sentiment continuation.
xaMzfArgut.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explaining alignment-retention differences beyond dataset size is relevant and that separating dataset geometry from representation geometry is potentially useful.
xaMzfArgut.main_concern: Reviewers consistently find the central conclusion theoretically unsupported, noting an apparent equation-direction contradiction and unjustified effective-volume factorization.

V83R4gRugB.one_liner: Corrects decentralized Riemannian stochastic recursive momentum with Hessian-vector products and metric projection on compact submanifolds.
V83R4gRugB.problem: Directly importing Euclidean Hessian-corrected momentum to manifolds fails because the tangent projector changes along iterates, altering the Riemannian gradient in ambient space.
V83R4gRugB.method: DPRSHCM pairs a correction for full ambient gradient variation with a projected iterate difference, combined with gradient tracking and metric projection using one stochastic gradient and one Hessian-vector product per node per iteration.
V83R4gRugB.key_idea: Compensates recursive momentum for changing tangent spaces using ambient Hessian-vector products, projected iterate differences, gradient tracking, and metric projection.
V83R4gRugB.evidence: Convergence proofs under diminishing and constant stepsizes, plus experiments on principal component analysis and regularized low-rank matrix completion.
V83R4gRugB.claimed_gains: Attains O~(epsilon^(-3/2)) per-node oracle complexity for expected squared Riemannian gradient norm and mean squared consensus error without knowing the iteration budget.
V83R4gRugB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric correction for changing tangent spaces is principled, well motivated, and backed by checkable theoretical derivations.
V83R4gRugB.main_concern: The low-rank matrix completion experiments fall outside the stated global smoothness assumptions, and the empirical benefit of the Hessian correction is not clearly isolated.

XmIXQ83u84.one_liner: Tests pre-generation linear hallucination probes across yes/no and free-form captioning under matched image, object, and sampling.
XmIXQ83u84.problem: Pre-generation hallucination probes report high AUROC on yes/no questions, but their transfer to free-form object captioning is untested.
XmIXQ83u84.method: The authors hold the model, image, queried object, and sampling fixed while varying only the instruction format, estimating hallucination propensity from 16 decodes and measuring probe AUROC recovery relative to an oracle.
XmIXQ83u84.key_idea: Compares pre-generation linear probe AUROC recovery across forced yes/no and free-caption prompts while holding image, target object, and sampling fixed.
XmIXQ83u84.evidence: Experiments across three vision-language models using human-verified absent objects, 16 sampled decodes, permutation tests, and layer/token/nonlinear readout controls.
XmIXQ83u84.claimed_gains: Probes recover 84 to 97% of attainable signal under forced yes/no versus 11 to 18% in free captions; naming the object restores 42 to 63%, and forced-choice states predict caption hallucination at 72 to 76% recovery.
XmIXQ83u84.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well-written and demonstrates through well-controlled paired comparisons that yes/no probe performance does not generalize to free-form captioning.
XmIXQ83u84.main_concern: The failure in free-form captions is confounded with the absence of target-object information in the prefill state and limited positive outcomes per seed.

a95I5CUxpn.one_liner: Subtracts shared KV-cache prefix footprint and applies Geometric Slicing Algorithm for non-clairvoyant decoding scheduling.
a95I5CUxpn.problem: Schedulers that cannot distinguish shared prefixes from disjoint prompts overcount KV-cache memory, causing an Omega(k) completion-time penalty.
a95I5CUxpn.method: For simultaneous requests sharing a resident prefix with no private suffixes, Coverage-GSA subtracts the shared KV footprint from the memory budget and schedules remaining generated tokens via staggered Geometric Slicing Algorithm retries.
a95I5CUxpn.key_idea: Reduces shared-prefix scheduling to residual generated-token scheduling by subtracting the resident prefix KV footprint and applying staggered doubling retries.
a95I5CUxpn.evidence: Competitive-ratio proofs, lower-bound and counterexample constructions, and Text Generation Inference (TGI) serving experiments on constructed and natural-language bursts.
a95I5CUxpn.claimed_gains: Achieves a 76/3 competitive ratio for total completion time and 1.43x and 1.95x makespan speedups in TGI on constructed and natural-language request bursts, respectively.
a95I5CUxpn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a well-motivated KV-cache scheduling problem with a clear lower bound, clean residual-budget reduction, and rigorous competitive analysis.
a95I5CUxpn.main_concern: The constant 76/3 competitive ratio is restricted to a single resident prefix without private suffixes, and the algorithmic novelty over prior GSA is incremental.

w0JCWG9GJd.one_liner: Jointly optimizes paid workflow cuts and individualized success bonuses to minimize commitment under worst-case equilibrium reliability.
w0JCWG9GJd.problem: Workflow dependencies increase the incentive cost of reliable multi-agent cooperation, while uniform bonuses are inefficient when agent services are heterogeneous.
w0JCWG9GJd.method: StructPay jointly selects paid workflow cuts (which remove predecessor dependencies) and individualized success bonuses to minimize total commitment at a fixed worst-case local-reliability target. It characterizes worst-case risk over approximate coarse correlated equilibria to enable certified optimization.
w0JCWG9GJd.key_idea: Minimizes incentive commitment by jointly choosing paid workflow dependency cuts and individualized bonuses under an exact worst-case coarse-correlated-equilibrium reliability characterization.
w0JCWG9GJd.evidence: Supported by equilibrium theorems, 300 frozen heterogeneous design instances, a 2,700-case continuation, and a two-agent LLM behavioral game.
w0JCWG9GJd.claimed_gains: StructPay achieves median commitment savings of 55.5% over optimized individual rewards on a fixed workflow and 18.1% over optimized structure with a common reward, and commits 21.4% less in the two-agent game.
w0JCWG9GJd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the exact worst-case coarse-correlated-equilibrium characterization and matching commitment bounds are substantial, well-structured theoretical contributions.
w0JCWG9GJd.main_concern: Reviewers note strong, unvalidated assumptions about public effort costs and clean workflow cuts, and observe that reoptimizing individual rewards on a common-bonus structure recovers most of the 18.1% joint gain.

URZcHDHt6i.one_liner: Studies which trajectory-level validity properties transfer from conditional training paths to learned flow-matching generators on Lie groups.
URZcHDHt6i.problem: Flow matching trains on conditional paths, but it is unclear which trajectory-level validity properties survive population marginalization, finite regression, and discrete sampling.
URZcHDHt6i.method: The authors analyze property transfer on Lie groups, proving that one-time marginals, terminal-state validity, expected additive costs, and almost-sure open-set avoidance transfer, whereas positive hitting probabilities do not. They run controlled experiments separating coupling, path design, regression, and sampling.
URZcHDHt6i.key_idea: Separates population marginalization, finite regression, and discrete sampling on Lie groups to characterize which conditional trajectory properties survive in flow-matching generators.
URZcHDHt6i.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs, population-oracle diagnostics, and controlled experiments on tori and rotation groups with Euclidean controls.
URZcHDHt6i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing conditional path properties from marginal flow and fitted generator properties is a useful perspective backed by clear analytic examples.
URZcHDHt6i.main_concern: Reviewers find the experimental section poorly organized and disconnected from the main goal, and question how much new insight is added beyond existing Rectified Flow theory.

J3aoJnseYG.one_liner: Audits test-time fast-weight updates in streaming 3D reconstruction (Scal3R) and finds they barely affect camera trajectory accuracy.
J3aoJnseYG.problem: Streaming 3D reconstruction models use test-time training (TTT) fast weights, but whether inference-time updates actually drive geometric accuracy is unclear.
J3aoJnseYG.method: The authors separate the architectural presence of the TTT branch from its test-time fast-weight updates in Scal3R by freezing fast weights and tracing gradient norms, Muon-style orthogonalization, and residual-stream dilution across layers.
J3aoJnseYG.key_idea: Freezing fast weights vs. removing the TTT branch reveals that Scal3R's TTT benefit arises during training while inference updates are neutralized by orthogonalization and residual dilution.
J3aoJnseYG.evidence: Audits Scal3R across 13 TUM, 7-Scenes, 1,200-frame windows, 10 ScanNet++, 11 KITTI, and Oxford Spires sequences.
J3aoJnseYG.claimed_gains: Freezing or removing TTT changes ATE by under 0.9% on TUM/7-Scenes, <=1.0% on 1,200-frame windows, 1.3% on ScanNet++, and 2.40% on KITTI (vs. 39% higher ATE when retrained without memory).
J3aoJnseYG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating TTT branch presence from inference-time weight updates is an important and carefully executed diagnostic.
J3aoJnseYG.main_concern: Reviewers note the audit examines only one released checkpoint (Scal3R), focuses mainly on pose ATE rather than depth/point clouds, and leaves the root cause of pose insensitivity partly open.

QHIRkouCS4.one_liner: Uses synthetic Python trace prediction (TinyTracer) and attention interventions to diagnose variable-renaming brittleness in code models.
QHIRkouCS4.problem: Decoder-only code models suffer prediction shifts under semantics-preserving variable renaming for poorly understood mechanistic reasons.
QHIRkouCS4.method: The authors introduce TinyTracer to generate synthetic Python execution traces under controlled variable-name diversity, train small decoder-only Transformers from scratch, and use head ablation and forced attention redirection alongside StarCoder probes to locate renaming failures.
QHIRkouCS4.key_idea: Low variable-name diversity during training causes models to fail at predicting unfamiliar variable boundaries, which can be partially repaired by redirecting copying attention heads.
QHIRkouCS4.evidence: Controlled variable-diversity training on TinyTracer, small-name-pool controls, head-ablation/attention-redirection interventions, and StarCoder evaluations.
QHIRkouCS4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled TinyTracer experiments, the small-name-pool control, and the causal head-ablation and attention-redirection analyses.
QHIRkouCS4.main_concern: Reviewers note that the causal link between copying heads and diversity-induced robustness gains is not fully established, and the discrepancy between TinyTracer (name endings) and StarCoder (name beginnings) remains unexplained.

y4l0mv8I9D.one_liner: Replaces pairwise preference steering with Reference-Grounded Steering (RGS) using constrained uplift, leakage, and energy penalties.
y4l0mv8I9D.problem: Pairwise preference objectives for representation steering can achieve positive margins via joint suppression or co-amplification rather than genuine uplift of the intended behavior.
y4l0mv8I9D.method: The authors formulate Reference-Grounded Steering (RGS), a soft-penalty objective that promotes intended-behavior uplift relative to an unsteered reference while penalizing separation violations, competing-behavior leakage, native-response drift, and intervention energy.
y4l0mv8I9D.key_idea: Constraining absolute score displacements relative to an unsteered reference across intended, alternative, and native response pools prevents pairwise margin hacking.
y4l0mv8I9D.evidence: Controlled experiments and evaluations across nine models from three families using teacher-forced scores and LLM-judged free generation.
y4l0mv8I9D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing relative preference ranking from selective behavioral control is well-motivated and insightful.
y4l0mv8I9D.main_concern: Reviewers point out that free-generation metrics still measure relative separation rather than absolute uplift over unsteered baselines, rely on a single LLM judge, and lack proof that teacher-forced constraints generalize to free generation.

tw9rh4fyrA.one_liner: Trains world models on sampled latent dimension or token prefixes so one model plans across compute budgets.
tw9rh4fyrA.problem: Conventional latent world models use a fixed latent size, forcing a fixed trade-off between representation capacity and rollout planning cost.
tw9rh4fyrA.method: NestedWM jointly trains an encoder and action-conditioned predictor over randomly sampled leading dimension or token prefixes, using each selected prefix as both predictor input and target space.
tw9rh4fyrA.key_idea: Samples leading latent dimension or token prefixes during joint encoder-predictor training so each prefix serves as input and prediction target.
tw9rh4fyrA.evidence: Dimension-wise and token-wise evaluations on visual-control and synthetic tasks (including PushT and Dot3), plus kNN probing and matched-predictor analyses.
tw9rh4fyrA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value enabling multiple planning budgets in one model and the thorough dimension-wise probing and matched-predictor analyses.
tw9rh4fyrA.main_concern: Token-wise comparisons confound nesting with pretrained full-budget initialization and teacher distillation, while dimension-wise experiments yield no compute savings.

ujpTOmuWpq.one_liner: Plans at deployment time over a 1D epigraph displacement family using short-horizon simulator rollouts and terminal values.
ujpTOmuWpq.problem: Epigraph-conditioned MARL controllers with fixed safety margins cannot adapt their safety-performance trade-off to individual deployment instances.
ujpTOmuWpq.method: EpiPlan parameterizes candidate policies by a scalar displacement from the state-dependent root and runs short-horizon simulations with learned terminal values before execution to select the best policy.
ujpTOmuWpq.key_idea: Searches over a one-dimensional epigraph displacement parameter at deployment time using short-horizon rollouts and terminal value estimates.
ujpTOmuWpq.evidence: Evaluations across 18 Def-MARL checkpoints on multi-agent control tasks (Corridor, Target, Line-5) with frozen splits and confidence intervals.
ujpTOmuWpq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note that EpiPlan is a simple, training-free post-hoc wrapper that improves safety-performance trade-offs on Def-MARL checkpoints.
ujpTOmuWpq.main_concern: Gains rely on privileged exact-simulator lookahead over the first 25% of deterministic episodes, and non-standard terminology makes the paper hard to follow.

wpLxpObES1.one_liner: Refines Attention Matching KV caches on hybrid LLMs via teacher-forced continuation distillation without synthetic question generation.
wpLxpObES1.problem: Learned KV-cache compression methods like self-study require expensive synthetic QA generation for each document before distilling into a compact cache.
wpLxpObES1.method: Neural Context Compiler (NCC) initializes a compact KV cache using Attention Matching and refines its keys and values by distilling the full-context hybrid teacher on teacher-forced continuations of the document's own text. This avoids text decoding and synthetic question generation.
wpLxpObES1.key_idea: Initializes a compact KV cache with Attention Matching and refines it by distilling full-context teacher logits on teacher-forced document continuations.
wpLxpObES1.evidence: Evaluated on hybrid Qwen3.6-27B across 64 held-out Qasper papers, four LongBench tasks, and 34K-97K-token documents against AM and self-study controls.
wpLxpObES1.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.6-27B, NCC raises Qasper F1 over AM from 38.1 to 44.2 and masked number recall from 62.3% to 79.8%, retaining 74-84% of full-context QA F1 at 11-30x compression.
wpLxpObES1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the generation-free continuation distillation method is simple, practical, and improves over Attention Matching on long documents.
wpLxpObES1.main_concern: Reviewers highlight evaluation on only a single hybrid model (Qwen3.6-27B), high per-document compilation overhead (20-41 minutes), and skewed comparisons to scaled-down self-study.

VeebM1PbSx.one_liner: Poisons vertical federated learning via consistent cluster-level feature swapping and defends by attributing and repairing the corrupted view.
VeebM1PbSx.problem: Passive parties in vertical federated learning can destabilize joint training without label access by corrupting cross-view sample correspondence.
VeebM1PbSx.method: The proposed Byzantine attack (CCVS) consistently swaps a passive party's features between distant latent clusters during training so the global model fails on clean aligned inference data. To defend, RGAR uses a trusted reference set to attribute the corrupted party and replace its representations rather than dropping the party.
VeebM1PbSx.key_idea: Permutes a passive party's embeddings between distant latent clusters to poison VFL cross-view correspondence, and defends via reference-guided party attribution and feature repair.
VeebM1PbSx.evidence: Evaluated across six public datasets varying swap coverage, auxiliary labels, party count, and reference-set size.
VeebM1PbSx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a realistic VFL-specific correspondence attack surface and evaluates it across multiple modalities and ablation factors.
VeebM1PbSx.main_concern: Reviewers flag an internal inconsistency in UCI-Bank H-ACC vs. Purity metrics, unisolated donor-selection ablations, and strong trusted-auditor assumptions for RGAR.

20mdu1pwMq.one_liner: Unlocks native FP8 E3M4 packing and MMA instructions on Blackwell GPUs with fused attention corrections.
20mdu1pwMq.problem: Standard FP8 E4M3 wastes an exponent bit under 32-element block scaling while sacrificing significand precision needed for accurate low-bit attention.
20mdu1pwMq.method: FreeAttn identifies and validates native packed F2FP conversion and block-scaled MMA instructions for E3M4 on Blackwell SM120, integrating them into a single-pass fused attention kernel with composable, shared-statistics error corrections.
20mdu1pwMq.key_idea: Uses native Blackwell E3M4 conversion and MMA instructions in a fused attention path with shared-statistics error corrections.
20mdu1pwMq.evidence: Evaluated on 32K language prefill (Qwen) and video generation (Wan2.1-14B) on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU.
20mdu1pwMq.claimed_gains: Accelerates 32K language prefill by 1.18-1.19x over BF16 Torch SDPA (1.89-1.97x in attention) and cuts distribution KL divergence by 2.4-4.3x relative to matched E4M3.
20mdu1pwMq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the native E3M4 instruction integration and controlled native-vs-software conversion benchmarks (4.6%-17.4% speedup).
20mdu1pwMq.main_concern: Reviewers note small end-to-end speedups over SageAttention2++ alongside higher KL divergence and lower video SSIM, plus mismatched correction settings.

kEU0L0Wtzs.one_liner: Introduces Fork-Invariance distillation with a gradient-norm cap so shared-cache world model branches retain diversity.
kEU0L0Wtzs.problem: Sharing a noisy KV cache across tree-structured world-model branches correlates continuations, causing under-dispersion that reduces best-of-k search gains.
kEU0L0Wtzs.method: The authors analyze shared-cache correlation in a linear-Gaussian model and propose Fork-Invariance, which matches noised-cache rollouts to clean-cache references using a shared sampling tape. To prevent quality degradation and prefix insensitivity, they cap the Fork-Invariance gradient norm at 0.2 of the distillation gradient.
kEU0L0Wtzs.key_idea: Distills noised-cache rollouts toward clean-cache references under a shared sampling tape while capping the objective's gradient norm at 0.2 of the distillation gradient.
kEU0L0Wtzs.evidence: Provides a linear-Gaussian theorem and experiments on a 1.4B distilled autoregressive video model (Self-Forcing / Wan2.1) measuring variance ratio, best-of-k search, visual judges, and prefix sensitivity.
kEU0L0Wtzs.claimed_gains: Increases cache-noise variance ratio to 0.888 (from 0.25 under high cache noise) without detected quality loss, and lifts retained best-of-k search gain from 52% to 84% at matched variance ratio.
kEU0L0Wtzs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that shared-cache under-dispersion in world-model branching is an interesting problem and appreciate the empirical analysis of training failure modes.
kEU0L0Wtzs.main_concern: Two reviewers argue the paper conflates exchangeability with conditional independence in its linear-Gaussian claim, while another notes narrow single-model scope and an ad-hoc gradient-cap workaround.

6RBd4ZKR4k.one_liner: Tests whether static incident snapshots predict live microservice root-cause analysis using a paired three-arm protocol and hash-locked prospective runs.
6RBd4ZKR4k.problem: Static snapshot benchmarks are standard for evaluating microservice RCA agents, but whether they predict live diagnostic performance is untested.
6RBd4ZKR4k.method: The authors introduce a paired protocol comparing Snapshot, Live-fixed (same cutoff on a live backend), and Live environments under three admissibility conditions, plus prospective validation of hash-locked snapshot success rates against fresh live incidents.
6RBd4ZKR4k.key_idea: Separates backend dynamics from observation-window effects using paired Snapshot, Live-fixed, and Live arms with machine-checkable admissibility conditions.
6RBd4ZKR4k.evidence: Evaluated on six fault specifications across two microservice applications with two models (including 120 prospective Live incidents).
6RBd4ZKR4k.claimed_gains: In prospective testing on 120 Live incidents, locked snapshot rates matched Live outcomes with a mean gap of -0.0125 (95% CI [-0.079, +0.054]).
6RBd4ZKR4k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of whether offline snapshots predict live RCA agent performance is important and like the three-arm decomposition.
6RBd4ZKR4k.main_concern: The primary paired analysis has only four admissible cases—failing to answer when snapshots predict live performance—and heavy internal codenames plus unresolved pipeline defects make the paper hard to read.

4Xpep6lt9c.one_liner: Introduces SITU, an 89,199-probe bilingual social-media benchmark, and studies retrieval and SFT for interpreting evolving UGC expressions.
4Xpep6lt9c.problem: Existing benchmarks test downstream labels or isolated phenomena rather than integrated interpretation of evolving expressions and conversational context in social UGC.
4Xpep6lt9c.method: SITU compiles 89,199 Chinese and English open-ended interpretation probes across nine categories (with 9,522 difficulty-filtered probes) and evaluates retrieval, expression oracles, SFT, and data scaling, plus unseen phonetic variants.
4Xpep6lt9c.key_idea: Combines expression-centered and context-integrative open-ended probes across bilingual social-media posts to diagnose and improve UGC understanding.
4Xpep6lt9c.evidence: Evaluated frontier models, retrieval, and SFT on SITU (89,199 probes; 554 held-out phonetic variants) and downstream translation and toxicity detection.
4Xpep6lt9c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SITU addresses a meaningful gap in evaluating LLM understanding of contextual social-media language at scale.
4Xpep6lt9c.main_concern: Probe generation and nine-category design lack clear justification and examples, evaluating against frozen references with same-family LLM judges raises validity concerns, and temporal/platform splits are underexplored.

LnQZuQQ15J.one_liner: Distilling future-conditioned gesture-token distributions into a causal generator uses training-time speech context without inference lookahead.
LnQZuQQ15J.problem: Causal co-speech gesture generation lacks future speech during deployment even though complete training recordings contain context that could improve supervision.
LnQZuQQ15J.method: ForeMotion shares an autoregressive discrete-gesture generator between a causal speech view and a future-conditioned view. A stop-gradient token-distillation loss trains the causal view to match future-informed predictive distributions over the same motion history.
LnQZuQQ15J.key_idea: Paired-view distillation transfers future-conditioned gesture-token distributions into the causal generator while executing only the causal view at inference.
LnQZuQQ15J.evidence: Experiments on BEATX include external baselines, causal controls, and separate single-speaker and multi-speaker evaluations discussed by reviewers.
LnQZuQQ15J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that privileged future context can improve causal training without adding runtime lookahead or extra inference overhead.
LnQZuQQ15J.main_concern: Two reviewers argue that matched future-speech benefits are not isolated from generic consistency regularization and that gains weaken in multi-speaker settings.

djN5Djcv3u.one_liner: Regularizes Vision Transformers for prediction consistency under gradient-guided attention perturbations to sharpen attention in small-data training.
djN5Djcv3u.problem: Vision Transformers trained from scratch on small datasets exhibit flatter attention, higher local sensitivity to attention perturbations, and poor generalization.
djN5Djcv3u.method: The authors analyze how bounded input shifts perturb attention logits and link sharp attention to a vanishing softmax Jacobian. They propose GRASP, a training-time regularizer that enforces prediction consistency under gradient-guided worst-case attention perturbations without adding inference overhead.
djN5Djcv3u.key_idea: Applies a training-only consistency loss under gradient-guided attention-logit perturbations to attenuate local sensitivity and implicitly sharpen attention.
djN5Djcv3u.evidence: Evaluated across ViT, PiT, and Swin architectures on six small datasets, ImageNet distribution-shift benchmarks, and downstream detection and segmentation tasks, plus local Jacobian sensitivity analysis.
djN5Djcv3u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the attention-sensitivity analysis, zero inference overhead, and consistent empirical improvements across ViT, PiT, and Swin on multiple datasets.
djN5Djcv3u.main_concern: Theoretical proofs rely on mismatched perturbation budgets and restrictive one-hot saturation assumptions that do not establish general entropy-sensitivity links, and training ViTs from scratch on small datasets is weakly motivated compared to fine-tuning foundation models.

MZxBh9ibVA.one_liner: Benchmarks custom load-balanced blocked-ELL dynamic sparse training kernels across six GPUs to model how SM count, clock, and dense baselines set speedups.
MZxBh9ibVA.problem: Mask-based dynamic sparse training still executes dense matrix products, and even hardware-sparse kernels exhibit wide unexplained speedup variation across GPUs.
MZxBh9ibVA.method: The authors build BlockDST, maintaining a constant number of live blocks per block-row so custom load-balanced blocked-ELL kernels execute all three per-layer products sparsely, including a block-SDDMM for weight gradients. They benchmark BlockDST and cuSPARSE's Blocked-ELL across six NVIDIA GPUs and fit a one-parameter SM-count-times-clock throughput model.
MZxBh9ibVA.key_idea: Executes all three dynamic sparse training layer GEMMs via load-balanced blocked-ELL kernels and models kernel throughput by SM count times clock frequency across six GPUs.
MZxBh9ibVA.evidence: Kernel benchmarks on six NVIDIA GPUs (including A100, A40, L40) comparing BlockDST, dense GEMM, and cuSPARSE Blocked-ELL, plus end-to-end training on a CIFAR-10 MLP.
MZxBh9ibVA.claimed_gains: Runs 1.08–5.13x faster than dense GEMM at 95% sparsity across six GPUs; the one-parameter model predicts held-out card throughput within 0.91–1.19x at the reference shape (0.78–1.66x across shapes); reaches fixed accuracy 1.49x faster on an L40.
MZxBh9ibVA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating kernel speed, step throughput, and time-to-accuracy across six GPU architectures with candid negative results is methodical and informative.
MZxBh9ibVA.main_concern: Reviewers note that the SM-count-times-clock model does not generalize to cuSPARSE Blocked-ELL, kernel novelty over prior hardware-aware DST work is unclear, and end-to-end tests are limited to a wide CIFAR-10 MLP.

G0PgGUA2UK.one_liner: Constructs optimal-transport relational graphs with support and challenge edges for conflict-aware multi-agent LLM message passing and trajectory verification.
G0PgGUA2UK.problem: Free-form multi-agent LLM debate and answer-level voting suffer from dominant-answer collapse, where wrong majorities suppress valid dissenting evidence.
G0PgGUA2UK.method: ARGOT represents agents' initial responses as evidence distributions and uses optimal transport to build a task-adaptive graph with typed support and challenge edges for conflict-aware message passing. A trajectory-level verifier then selects the final answer by inspecting routed evidence trajectories instead of relying on answer frequency.
G0PgGUA2UK.key_idea: Uses optimal transport over agent response distributions to build typed support-and-challenge graphs for conflict-aware message passing followed by trajectory-level verification.
G0PgGUA2UK.evidence: Evaluated across six reasoning benchmarks (including MedMCQA, MMLU-Pro, AIME, HumanEval) with minority-rescue analyses and ablations.
G0PgGUA2UK.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest average performance across six reasoning benchmarks and ranks first on four tasks.
G0PgGUA2UK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preventing dominant-answer collapse and protecting minority reasoning via typed support/challenge edges is well motivated and directly analyzed.
G0PgGUA2UK.main_concern: Reviewers flag internal inconsistencies in reported benchmark numbers, unisolated necessity of optimal transport (which only uses option and confidence) versus the trajectory verifier, and missing token/latency cost comparisons.

oWnat9npx3.one_liner: Audits accumulated streaming time-series data via causal local affine probes and simultaneous confidence bounds on risk quasiconvexity to choose retraining size.
oWnat9npx3.problem: Streaming time-series predictors must choose how much post-drift data to accumulate before retraining without knowing future update benefit or retraining at every candidate size.
oWnat9npx3.method: RETICLE fits causal local affine probes in a frozen representation across a bandwidth grid and tests whether the resulting risk profile satisfies approximate quasiconvexity, a necessary condition for finite-sample local-learning regularity. Using simultaneous confidence bounds valid under temporal dependence, it selects the first checkpoint that passes certification without retraining the downstream model.
oWnat9npx3.key_idea: Certifies approximate quasiconvexity of causal local-probe risk across bandwidths with simultaneous confidence bounds to trigger streaming model retraining without trial retraining.
oWnat9npx3.evidence: Evaluated on checkpoint selection across 3 synthetic systems and 16 real cases with 6 learners, plus continuous fine-tuning on 3 forecasting datasets with 2 drift detectors across 5 seeds.
oWnat9npx3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that selecting post-drift update data size is a practical problem and that RETICLE provides a statistically principled formulation tested across many learners and settings.
oWnat9npx3.main_concern: Reviewers note heavy, hard-to-follow notation, an indirect link between certifying local-probe quasiconvexity and downstream retraining improvement, and reproducibility issues (inaccessible code and missing variance in Table 1).

KL3GMYps6X.one_liner: Introduces a multi-signal research-idea evaluation benchmark and trains a dedicated reward model on automated preference pairs.
KL3GMYps6X.problem: As LLMs generate research ideas at scale, reliably evaluating and selecting strong ideas before execution remains a bottleneck where existing evaluators perform poorly.
KL3GMYps6X.method: The authors build IdeaRewardBench, a semiannually updated benchmark of 3,185 preference instances grounded in peer-review, citation-impact, and human-annotation signals. They also train IdeaReward, a dedicated reward model learned from over 20,000 automated idea preference pairs.
KL3GMYps6X.key_idea: Constructs a multi-signal benchmark combining review, citation, and annotation signals and trains a dedicated research-idea reward model on 20,000+ automated preference pairs.
KL3GMYps6X.evidence: Evaluates 23 baselines (general reward models, LLM judges, and specialized evaluators) and IdeaReward on IdeaRewardBench's 3,185 preference instances.
KL3GMYps6X.claimed_gains: The best evaluated baseline achieves only 62.8% pairwise accuracy on the review-grounded split and 60.9% on the impact-grounded split (50% random); IdeaReward's exact gain numbers are not stated in the abstract excerpt.
KL3GMYps6X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a shared multi-horizon benchmark combining review, impact, and annotation signals with broad 23-baseline coverage addresses a timely evaluation gap.
KL3GMYps6X.main_concern: Reviewers question using full-paper acceptance and raw citations as noisy proxies for extracted idea cards (with minimal human validation), AI/ML-only scope, and missing comparison to prior idea-reward work.

24Vycg3qsh.one_liner: Defines intent multiplicity and introduces a real cloud-ticket benchmark showing agent degradation as distinct dialogue intents grow.
24Vycg3qsh.problem: Existing analyses attribute multi-turn LLM-agent degradation to dialogue length alone, obscuring how multiple distinct user intents drive failures.
24Vycg3qsh.method: The authors formalize intent multiplicity as the number of distinct annotated user intents in a dialogue history and introduce CloudIntent-Bench, built from authentic cloud-service support tickets. They evaluate frontier LLMs across intent-multiplicity regimes and run controlled interventions that remove irrelevant history or provide intent hints.
24Vycg3qsh.key_idea: Characterizes dialogue difficulty via intent multiplicity—the count of distinct user intents—and isolates its effect on agent decisions using real cloud support tickets and controlled intent interventions.
24Vycg3qsh.evidence: Evaluates multiple frontier models on CloudIntent-Bench (1,973 decision tasks from 1,766 real cloud support tickets) plus controlled 100-task intent-removal and intent-hint studies.
24Vycg3qsh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding the benchmark in authentic cloud support tickets and separating intent multiplicity from raw conversation length is realistic and well motivated.
24Vycg3qsh.main_concern: Reviewers note underspecified dataset construction, reliance on an unverified 32B model for intent counts (76.4% exact agreement on full tickets), and that raw intent count is a coarse metric.

OLGULSDMlA.one_liner: Transfers language-calibrated brain-atlas connectivity priors from unimodal fMRI cohorts into a dual-branch multimodal fMRI-DTI network.
OLGULSDMlA.problem: Multimodal brain network learning from paired fMRI and DTI data is limited by small paired sample sizes, while modality gaps hinder direct transfer from larger fMRI-only cohorts.
OLGULSDMlA.method: SCMT uses atlas-defined brain regions as a shared interface, calibrating language-derived regional descriptions with source fMRI connectivity and diagnosis supervision to extract regional affinities and a healthy-connectivity reference. A dual-branch reconstruction model combines paired structure-function data with a prior-guided auxiliary functional branch under an annealed consistency loss.
OLGULSDMlA.key_idea: Transfers architecture-independent ROI-level affinity and healthy-connectivity priors calibrated from language descriptions and unimodal fMRI cohorts into a dual-branch multimodal model via annealed consistency.
OLGULSDMlA.evidence: Evaluated on ABIDE I and ADNI under label-blind transductive adaptation with ablation, fusion, and source-scale analyses.
OLGULSDMlA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transferring lightweight, architecture-independent ROI-level priors across an atlas interface is a sensible, well-motivated approach to paired neuroimaging scarcity.
OLGULSDMlA.main_concern: Reviewers flag high performance variance without statistical significance tests, metric inconsistencies on ADNI (Macro-F1 above accuracy), unisolated 50.6% parameter increase, and outdated baselines.

0xrunFu3MG.one_liner: Controls adaptive evidence retrieval for recommendation agents via a gate-before-scoring continuous bandit learned offline.
0xrunFu3MG.problem: Recommendation rerankers cannot recover unretrieved items, while indiscriminate retrieval expansion wastes compute budgets.
0xrunFu3MG.method: ECB uses a gate-before-scoring controller that inspects a base recommender's output to decide whether to trigger exploration. When triggered, an Evidence-aware Ranker produces candidate signals that condition a continuous bandit policy governing interest focus, evidence mixing, and source allocation, trained offline with a target-conditioned proxy reward.
0xrunFu3MG.key_idea: Gates retrieval expansion before scoring and uses candidate-level evidence signals to condition an offline-trained continuous bandit policy over interest focus, evidence mixing, and source allocation.
0xrunFu3MG.evidence: Evaluated on four recommendation datasets on top of OneRec with matched-round gating and budget-sensitivity ablations.
0xrunFu3MG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing retrieval-cost-aware candidate expansion with a gate-before-scoring mechanism and matched-budget ablations is well motivated and improves coverage and NDCG@5.
0xrunFu3MG.main_concern: Reviewers note missing implementation and training details for the learned proxy reward model and action distributions, unclear framing between tool use and continuous actions, and limited algorithmic novelty.

ryrADOtcDR.one_liner: Infers image metaphors via a training-free Perception-Search-Reasoning pipeline that retrieves missing cultural and contextual knowledge.
ryrADOtcDR.problem: Multimodal LLMs fail on visual metaphors because implied meanings depend on missing cultural and social context absent from raw pixels.
ryrADOtcDR.method: Let Androids Dream (LAD) is a training-free test-time pipeline with three stages: Perception extracts compositional visual structure, Search retrieves missing external context guided by perception, and Reasoning aligns visual compositions with retrieved context to infer emergent implications.
ryrADOtcDR.key_idea: Operationalizes contextual alignment at test time through three sequential stages—compositional visual perception, perception-guided web retrieval, and context-aligned reasoning—without model training.
ryrADOtcDR.evidence: Evaluated on S100 (100 English and Chinese implication questions), full II-Bench and CII-Bench, and general VQA across four vision-language backbones.
ryrADOtcDR.claimed_gains: On S100, raises GPT-4o-mini MCQ accuracy from 44% to 74% (English) and 42% to 52% (Chinese), and OSQ scores from 2.98 to 4.02 (English) and 3.36 to 3.66 (Chinese).
ryrADOtcDR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating perception, context retrieval, and reasoning is an intuitive, inspectable training-free approach to visual metaphor understanding.
ryrADOtcDR.main_concern: Reviewers point out that prompting alone accounts for much of the gain (removing search still jumps from 44 to 68), comparisons lack matched inference budgets, and gains shrink sharply on stronger backbones.

owvLYlVH0T.one_liner: Jointly optimizes multi-agent LLM reasoning and latent KV-cache communication via parameter-efficient end-to-end supervised training.
owvLYlVH0T.problem: Multi-agent LLM frameworks treat inter-agent communication as a fixed text or latent interface rather than jointly optimizing how agents encode and interpret messages.
owvLYlVH0T.method: DiffMAS performs parameter-efficient supervised fine-tuning over differentiable multi-agent latent KV-cache trajectories so agents jointly learn message encoding, interpretation, and reasoning end to end.
owvLYlVH0T.key_idea: Backpropagates supervised task loss end to end through differentiable latent KV-cache exchanges across agents using shared parameter-efficient adapters.
owvLYlVH0T.evidence: Evaluated across five LLM backbones and six mathematical reasoning, scientific QA, code generation, and commonsense benchmarks against single-agent, text-based, and latent multi-agent baselines with matched SFT controls.
owvLYlVH0T.claimed_gains: Achieves +26.7% on AIME24 and +20.2% on GPQA-Diamond, outperforming matched single-agent and text-based fine-tuned pipelines in 26 of 30 settings and never performing worse.
owvLYlVH0T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that end-to-end optimization of latent inter-agent communication is a meaningful direction backed by thorough, matched SFT controls across five backbones and six benchmarks.
owvLYlVH0T.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty over LatentMAS and Interlat, lack of a causal control isolating cross-agent gradient flow, requirement of task-specific adapters, and unclear cross-backbone applicability.

xF3nXCr2NY.one_liner: Extends federated TD learning to categorical return distributions with linear approximation using global control variates for variance reduction.
xF3nXCr2NY.problem: Existing federated reinforcement learning algorithms estimate only expected returns, failing to capture return uncertainty and risk needed for risk-sensitive decisions.
xF3nXCr2NY.method: FedVR-DistTD performs federated categorical distributional TD learning with linear function approximation, combining a global server control direction with same-sample TD differences to reduce client update variance. The authors prove finite-time convergence bounds for both last-iterate and tail-averaged server iterates.
xF3nXCr2NY.key_idea: Applies a global control direction and same-sample TD differences to reduce variance in federated categorical distributional TD learning with linear function approximation.
xF3nXCr2NY.evidence: Provides finite-time theoretical analysis under i.i.d. stationary generative-model sampling with homogeneous clients and full participation, plus an illustrative four-state Markov reward process experiment.
xF3nXCr2NY.claimed_gains: Tail-averaged server iterates converge to the linear-categorical projected fixed point at a root-mean-square rate of O(T^{-1/2}) for fixed N, B, and E.
xF3nXCr2NY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating variance-reduced federated distributional policy evaluation with linear function approximation and finite-time analysis is clean and theoretically relevant.
xF3nXCr2NY.main_concern: Reviewers flag a contradiction between claiming Markovian sampling in the introduction while assuming i.i.d. homogeneous full-participation sampling, limited novelty over federated linear SA, and a toy four-state evaluation.

8liuY2DA1V.one_liner: Compresses heterogeneous robot joint-graph trajectories via virtual-joint discrete tokenization and generates actions with delayed grouped autoregression.
8liuY2DA1V.problem: Cross-embodiment robot policies need compact action representations that preserve joint-level kinematics across diverse robot morphologies without predicting many correlated targets one by one.
8liuY2DA1V.method: HoloBrain-Discrete places virtual-joint bottleneck nodes on a robot's joint graph to compress trajectories into discrete codes via a shared encoder-decoder across embodiments. A code/cue delayed autoregressive policy predicts code groups along temporal, virtual-joint, and coarse-to-fine axes using per-code prediction cues.
8liuY2DA1V.key_idea: Uses robot-graph virtual-joint bottlenecks to discretize actions across embodiments and decodes code groups via delayed autoregression with separate per-code prediction cues.
8liuY2DA1V.evidence: Pretrained on roughly 10,000 hours across 18 robot embodiments and evaluated across six settings, RoboTwin, Aloha, LIBERO, and seven real-world manipulation tasks against diffusion-based HoloBrain.
8liuY2DA1V.claimed_gains: Outperforms diffusion-based HoloBrain at every measured pretraining checkpoint across six settings, and a diffusion head initialized from pretrained weights reaches 91.01 progress points on seven real tasks versus 85.30 for HoloBrain.
8liuY2DA1V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that virtual-joint action tokenization offers a useful, fast cross-embodiment representation that handles varying joint counts with a single shared encoder-decoder.
8liuY2DA1V.main_concern: Reviewers note that pretraining gains do not consistently carry over to post-training real-world performance, multiple design changes confound what drives pretraining gains, and competing tokenizer FASTer is omitted.

0VuEph4EFM.one_liner: Benchmarks MLE agent harnesses under matched models, hardware, and time budgets against a minimal coding-agent baseline.
0VuEph4EFM.problem: Published autonomous ML engineering agent gains confound backbone models, hardware, and elaborate orchestration harnesses, leaving the marginal value of MLE-specific harnesses unclear.
0VuEph4EFM.method: The authors run controlled, equal-time-budget comparisons of released MLE harnesses against a single-session minimal-harness coding agent baseline (Malena on OpenCode) using open-source frontier backbones, complemented by systematic harness ablations.
0VuEph4EFM.key_idea: Holds backbone model, GPU hardware, and wall-clock time budget fixed to isolate whether specialized MLE orchestration harnesses outperform a minimal read/write/bash coding-agent session.
0VuEph4EFM.evidence: Evaluated on MLE-bench across multiple open-weight frontier backbones (including GLM 5.2 and DeepSeek V4 Flash) and four external MLE harnesses with paired-by-task bootstrap confidence intervals and ablations.
0VuEph4EFM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that matched-backbone, matched-budget evaluation of MLE harnesses addresses an important attribution gap and provides credible comparative evidence.
0VuEph4EFM.main_concern: Reviewers argue the negative claims exceed the statistical and experimental evidence—Malena still relies on a full coding runtime (OpenCode), closed-model harnesses were ported to open weights, and post-training claims lack causal proof.

4nkKYSStp4.one_liner: Introduces a 502-task, guaranteed-solvable multi-turn benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on small molecule drug design.
4nkKYSStp4.problem: Existing evaluations of LLM agents for small molecule drug design are ad hoc, overly simple, small-scale, or limited to single-turn QA.
4nkKYSStp4.method: SMDD-Bench constructs 502 guaranteed-solvable, multi-turn tasks across 102 protein targets covering 2D Pharmacophore Identification, Interaction Point Discovery, Scaffold Hopping, Lead Optimization, and Fragment Assembly under a bounded oracle-call budget.
4nkKYSStp4.key_idea: Build guaranteed-solvable multi-turn small-molecule drug-design tasks around known feasible witness molecules across five medicinal-chemistry workflows and 102 protein targets.
4nkKYSStp4.evidence: Benchmarked seven open- and closed-source frontier LLMs with failure-mode analysis.
4nkKYSStp4.claimed_gains: Even the strongest evaluated LLM, GPT5.4, solves only 40.2% of SMDD-Bench tasks.
4nkKYSStp4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the five medicinal-chemistry task types are practically relevant and that constructing tasks around feasible witness molecules provides a solid, human-free evaluation basis.
4nkKYSStp4.main_concern: Reviewers note that binary all-constraint scoring gives near-zero resolution on hard tasks, baselines omit newer models and stronger agent scaffolds, and real-world chemical validity of oracle wins is unverified.

tunVuLrXNu.one_liner: Diagnoses late-layer FFN overcommitment via direct logit attribution and subtracts positive late FFN logit writes during MLLM decoding.
tunVuLrXNu.problem: Training-free hallucination decoding methods often suppress present objects alongside hallucinated ones because layer-level interventions rescale opposing attention and FFN effects together.
tunVuLrXNu.method: Using direct logit attribution across four MLLMs, the authors find that late-layer attention supports present objects while late FFNs promote image-insensitive hallucinated objects. They propose Component-wise Contrastive Decoding (CCD), which subtracts only positive late-layer FFN logit contributions in a single pass without training.
tunVuLrXNu.key_idea: Subtract only positive late-layer FFN direct-logit contributions from output logits in one pass to curb image-insensitive hallucinations without weakening visual attention support.
tunVuLrXNu.evidence: Direct logit attribution, progressive image-occlusion tests, and decoding evaluations across four pre-norm decoder-only MLLMs.
tunVuLrXNu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear sublayer-level diagnosis backed by occlusion controls and the simple, single-pass, training-free intervention.
tunVuLrXNu.main_concern: Reviewers highlight substantial overlap with prior attention-vs-FFN hallucination work (ReDeEP/AARF and FADE), limited coverage beyond four pre-norm decoder architectures, and limits of direct logit attribution for causality.
